title.en: Volume 55 Biographies 45: Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, Xi Chanwen, Xiao Houxiang, Shi Zhan, Cai Daogong, Yan Gongze, Deng Yuanqi, Zhang Huishao, Feng Daogen, Kang Xuan, Chang Yizhi
title.raw: 卷五十五 列傳第四十五 王茂 曹景宗 席闡文 夏侯詳 士瞻 蔡道恭 楊公則 鄧元起 張惠紹 馮道根 康絢 昌義之 Volume 55 Biographies 45: Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, Xi Chanwen, Xiao Houxiang, Shi Zhan, Cai Daogong, Yan Gongze, Deng Yuanqi, Zhang Huishao, Feng Daogen, Kang Xuan, Chang Yizhi

sentences.zh: 王茂字休連，一字茂先，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Mao, styled Xiulian and also Maoxian, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao, courtesy name Xiulian (also known as Maoxian), came from Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖深，北中郎司馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shen was Northern Central Commandant Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shen served as marshal of the Northern Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 父天生，宋末為列將，克司徒袁粲，以勳歷位郡守，封上黃縣男。

translations.literal: His father Tiansheng, in the late Song a ranked general, captured Grand Tutor Yuan Can, and through merit rose to command a prefecture; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Shanghuang County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Tiansheng, a ranked general in the late Song, took Grand Tutor Yuan Can and, for his merit, rose through prefectural posts until enfeoffed as Baron of Shanghuang.

sentences.zh: 茂年數歲，為大父深所異，常曰：「此吾家千里駒，成門戶者必此兒也。」

translations.literal: When Mao was several years old, his grandfather Shen regarded him as extraordinary and often said, "This is our family's thousand-li colt; the one who will uphold our house must be this boy."
translations.idiomatic: While Mao was still a child, his grandfather Shen singled him out and would say, "Here is the swift colt of our clan—the boy who will carry our house will be this one."

sentences.zh: 及長，好讀兵書，究其大指。

translations.literal: When grown, he loved reading military books and pursued their main purport.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown, he studied military texts and mastered their essential meaning.

sentences.zh: 性隱不交遊，身長八尺，潔白美容儀。

translations.literal: His nature was retiring and he did not mix in society; he stood eight chi tall, fair and handsome in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Reserved by nature and seldom social, he stood eight feet tall, with a fair complexion and striking looks.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝布衣時嘗見之，歎曰：「王茂先年少堂堂如此，必為公輔。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Qi was still in common dress he once saw him and sighed, "Wang Maoxian is so young and already so imposing—he will surely become a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi, still a commoner, once saw him and exclaimed, "Wang Maoxian is young yet already so commanding—he is bound for the highest offices."

sentences.zh: 後為台郎，累年不調。

translations.literal: Later he became a capital bureau gentleman but for many years received no promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as a capital bureau officer but went years without advancement.

sentences.zh: 亦知齊之將亡，求為邊職。

translations.literal: He also knew Qi was about to perish and sought a frontier post.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Qi was nearing collapse, he asked for a border appointment.

sentences.zh: 久之，為雍州長史、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: After a long while he became Chief Administrator of Yong Province and Administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made chief administrator of Yong Province and prefect of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 梁武便以王佐許之，事無大小皆詢焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang already treated him as a chief aide; matters great and small were all referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wudi already counted him among his chief advisers and consulted him on every matter, large or small.

sentences.zh: 人或譖茂反，帝弗之信。

translations.literal: Some slandered Mao as plotting rebellion, but the Emperor did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: When others accused Mao of rebellion, the emperor refused to credit it.

sentences.zh: 譖者驟言之，遣視其甲矟，則蟲網焉，乃誅言者。

translations.literal: The slanderers spoke repeatedly; he sent men to inspect Mao's armor and spears, and they were cobwebbed—then he executed the accusers.
translations.idiomatic: The accusers kept at it until he inspected Mao's arms and armor and found them draped in cobwebs; the informers were then put to death.

sentences.zh: 或云茂與帝不睦，帝諸腹心並勸除之。

translations.literal: Some said Mao and the Emperor were at odds, and all the Emperor's intimates urged removing him.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Mao and the emperor were estranged, and the inner circle urged his removal.

sentences.zh: 而茂少有驍名，帝又惜其用，曰：「將舉大事，便害健將，此非上策。」

translations.literal: But Mao had early won a name for valor, and the Emperor also valued his use, saying, "When about to undertake a great affair, to harm a stalwart general—this is no superior stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Mao's early fame for valor made the emperor reluctant to lose him: "To strike down a proven commander just as we raise a great enterprise is no wise policy."

sentences.zh: 乃令腹心鄭紹叔往候之。

translations.literal: He therefore sent his intimate Zheng Shaoshu to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his trusted follower Zheng Shaoshu to visit him instead.

sentences.zh: 遇其臥，因問疾。

translations.literal: He found him abed and inquired after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu found him in bed and asked after his health.

sentences.zh: 茂曰：「我病可耳。」

translations.literal: Mao said, "My illness is nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Mao replied, "I am hardly ill at all."

sentences.zh: 紹叔曰：「都下殺害日甚，使君家門塗炭，今欲起義，長史那猶臥。」

translations.literal: Shaoshu said, "In the capital killings grow daily and your house is scorched; now we wish to raise the righteous cause—how can the Chief Administrator still lie abed?"
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshu said, "Slaughter in the capital blackens your family's door; we mean to rise—how can you, Chief Administrator, still lie here?"

sentences.zh: 茂因擲枕起，即袴褶隨紹叔入見。

translations.literal: Mao thereupon flung aside his pillow and rose, donned jacket and trousers, and followed Shaoshu in to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Mao threw off his pillow, dressed at once, and went in with Shaoshu to see the emperor.

sentences.zh: 武帝大喜，下床迎，因結兄弟，被推赤心，遂得盡力。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased, came down from the couch to welcome him, bound brotherhood with him, was won by his open heart, and thus gained his full effort.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi was overjoyed, came down to receive him, swore brotherhood, won his wholehearted loyalty, and thereafter had his full strength.

sentences.zh: 發雍部，遣茂為前驅。

translations.literal: When Yong was mobilized, Mao was sent as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yong region marched, Mao led the van.

sentences.zh: 郢、魯既平，從武帝東下為軍鋒。

translations.literal: After Ying and Lu were pacified, he followed the Emperor east as army point.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ying and Lu had fallen, he marched east with Wudi as the army's spearhead.

sentences.zh: 師次秣陵，東昏遣大將王珍國盛兵朱雀門，眾號二十萬。

translations.literal: The army halted at Moling; Dong Hun sent Grand General Wang Zhenguo with a massive force at the Vermilion Bird Gate, the host claiming two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The host halted at Moling; Dong Hun's general Wang Zhenguo massed troops at the Vermilion Bird Gate, claiming two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 及戰，梁武軍引卻，茂下馬單刀直前，外甥韋欣慶勇力絕人，執鐵纏矟翼茂而進，故大破之。

translations.literal: In battle, Liang Wudi's army drew back; Mao dismounted and with a single blade pressed straight forward; his nephew Wei Xinqing, whose courage and strength were unmatched, wielded an iron-wrapped spear to shield Mao's advance—thus they routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When battle came, Wudi's line gave ground; Mao dismounted and charged alone with one blade while his nephew Wei Xinqing, a man of terrifying strength, bore a iron-bound spear to cover him—together they broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 茂勳第一，欣慶力也。

translations.literal: Mao's merit ranked first; Xinqing's strength had done it.
translations.idiomatic: Mao took first merit, though the credit was Xinqing's strength.

sentences.zh: 建康城平，以茂為護軍將軍，遷侍中、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Mao was made General Who Guards the Army, then moved to Palace Attendant and General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiankang fell, he was made General Who Guards the Army, then palace attendant and general who leads the army.

sentences.zh: 時東昏妃潘玉兒有國色，武帝將留之，以問茂。

translations.literal: At the time Dong Hun's consort Pan Yu'er had national beauty; the Emperor was about to keep her and asked Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun's consort Pan Yu'er was famed for her beauty; Wudi meant to keep her and asked Mao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 茂曰：「亡齊者此物，留之恐貽外議。」

translations.literal: Mao said, "Qi perished because of this creature; to keep her would fear outside criticism."
translations.idiomatic: Mao said, "This woman helped destroy Qi; keeping her will invite scandal."

sentences.zh: 帝乃出之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then released her.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi sent her away.

sentences.zh: 軍主田安啟求為婦，玉兒泣曰：「昔者見遇時主，今豈下匹非類。

translations.literal: Army commander Tian An memorialized asking her as wife; Yu'er wept, "Once I was favored by the ruler of the age—how could I now wed beneath my kind.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Tian An petitioned to marry her; Yu'er wept, "I was once the lord's chosen—how could I now be matched to my inferiors?

sentences.zh: 死而後已，義不受辱。」

translations.literal: I would die before I would accept disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: I will die rather than suffer dishonor."

sentences.zh: 及見縊，潔美如生。

translations.literal: When she was seen strangled, she was fair and beautiful as in life.
translations.idiomatic: When they found her hanged, she looked as fair as though still alive.

sentences.zh: 輿出，尉吏俱行非禮。

translations.literal: When the bier went out, escort officers all committed improprieties.
translations.idiomatic: As her coffin left the city, the escort guards behaved indecently toward her.

sentences.zh: 乃以餘妃賜茂，亦潘之亞也。

translations.literal: He then gave Mao a lesser consort, also second only to Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi therefore gave Mao another palace lady, nearly Pan's equal in beauty.

sentences.zh: 群盜之燒神獸門，茂率所領應赴，為盜所射。

translations.literal: When bandits burned the Divine Beast Gate, Mao led his command to respond and was shot by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When rioters torched the Divine Beast Gate, Mao led his men to the scene and was shot.

sentences.zh: 茂躍馬而進，群盜反走。

translations.literal: Mao leapt his horse forward and the bandits turned and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred forward and the mob scattered.

sentences.zh: 茂以不能式遏奸盜，自表解職，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Mao, holding himself unable to restrain wicked bandits, memorialized to resign; an excellent edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Unable, he felt, to check such lawlessness, he asked to resign; the emperor refused with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 加鎮軍將軍，封望蔡縣公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army and enfeoffed Duke of Wangcai County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and made Duke of Wangcai.

sentences.zh: 是歲，江州刺史陳伯之叛，茂出為江州刺史，南討之。

translations.literal: That year Jiangzhou Inspector Chen Bozhi rebelled; Mao went out as Jiangzhou Inspector to campaign south.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chen Bozhi, inspector of Jiangzhou, rebelled; Mao was sent south as inspector to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 伯之奔魏。

translations.literal: Bozhi fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi fled north to Wei.

sentences.zh: 時九江新經軍寇，茂務農省役，百姓安之。

translations.literal: At the time Jiujiang had newly suffered military ravage; Mao devoted himself to farming and lightening corvée, and the people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang had just been ravaged by war; Mao promoted farming, eased labor, and the people grew calm.

sentences.zh: 四年，魏攻漢中，茂受詔西禦，魏乃班師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wei attacked Hanzhong; Mao received orders to defend west and Wei then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Wei attacked Hanzhong; Mao marched west on imperial orders and the Wei army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 歷位侍中，中衛將軍，太子詹事，車騎將軍，開府儀同三司，丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He successively held Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, Crown Prince Household Steward, Chariots-and-Cavalry General, equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies with an opening office, and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through palace attendant, central guard general, crown prince's household steward, chariots-and-cavalry general, ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies with an opening office, and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，武帝方敦文雅，茂心頗怏怏，侍宴醉後，每見言色。

translations.literal: When the realm was at peace the Emperor was cultivating letters; Mao's heart was somewhat discontent, and after feasting drunk he often showed it in word and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: In a peaceful age Wudi turned to culture; Mao grew restless and, drunk at court, let his displeasure show.

sentences.zh: 武帝宥而不責。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned and did not reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi overlooked it without rebuke.

sentences.zh: 進位司空。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 茂性寬厚，居官雖無美譽，亦為吏人所安。

translations.literal: Mao's nature was generous and thick; in office though without fine reputation, officials and people were also at ease with him.
translations.idiomatic: Broad and forbearing, he won no special praise in office yet left clerks and commoners at ease.

sentences.zh: 居處方正，在一室衣冠儼然，雖僕妾莫見其惰容。

translations.literal: In dwelling he was upright; within a single room he was cap and gown in full order—even servant girls never saw him slack.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was exacting: even alone in a room he remained fully dressed, and servants never saw him careless.

sentences.zh: 姿表瑰麗，鬚眉如畫，為眾所瞻望。

translations.literal: His bearing was magnificent; beard and brows like painting—what all looked up to.
translations.idiomatic: His looks were splendid, beard and brows as if painted, and men gazed on him in admiration.

sentences.zh: 徙驃騎將軍、開府同三司之儀、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Rapid Cavalry General, ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, and Jiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to rapid-cavalry general with Three Excellency ceremony and made inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州不取奉，獄無滯囚，居處被服，同於儒者。

translations.literal: In the province he took no salary surplus; prisons held no long-detained prisoners; dwelling and dress were like a Confucian scholar's.
translations.idiomatic: In office he took no extra income, kept no prisoners languishing in jail, and lived as plainly as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 薨於州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in post.

sentences.zh: 武帝甚悼惜之，詔贈太尉，諡曰忠烈公。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply mourned him, edict-posthumously Minister of Works, posthumous title Loyal and Fierce Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi mourned him deeply, posthumously made him grand minister of works, and gave the posthumous name Loyal and Fierce Duke.

sentences.zh: 初，茂以元勳，武帝賜鍾磬之樂。

translations.literal: Earlier, for his founding merit the Emperor had bestowed bells and chimes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as a founding merit, Wudi had granted him bells and stone chimes.

sentences.zh: 茂在州，夢鍾磬在格，無故自墮，心惡之。

translations.literal: While Mao was in the province he dreamed the bells and chimes on the rack fell of themselves; his heart hated it.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he dreamed the instruments on their frame fell without cause and took it as ill omen.

sentences.zh: 及覺，命奏樂，既成列，鍾磬在格，果無故編皆絕墮地。

translations.literal: On waking he ordered music played; when the array was set, the bells and chimes on the rack indeed all broke their cords and fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Awake, he ordered them played; as the musicians formed ranks, every cord on the rack snapped and the pieces crashed down.

sentences.zh: 茂謂長史江詮曰：「此樂，天子所以惠勞臣也。

translations.literal: Mao said to Chief Administrator Jiang Quan, "This music is what the Son of Heaven bestowed to comfort and honor a minister.
translations.idiomatic: He told his chief administrator Jiang Quan, "These are the Son of Heaven's gift to reward a servant.

sentences.zh: 樂既極矣，能無憂乎。」

translations.literal: Music has reached its limit—can there be no sorrow?"
translations.idiomatic: When music reaches its height, can sorrow be far behind?"

sentences.zh: 俄而病卒。

translations.literal: Shortly after he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子貞秀嗣，以居憂無禮，為有司所奏，徙越州，後詔留廣州。

translations.literal: His son Zhenxiu succeeded; for impropriety in mourning he was memorialized by the authorities, banished to Yuezhou, later edict retained at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhenxiu inherited; for breaches of mourning ritual the authorities impeached him, exiled him to Yuezhou, then an edict kept him at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 與魏降人杜景欲襲州城，刺史蕭昂斬之。

translations.literal: With the Wei surrenderer Du Jing he plotted to seize the prefectural city; Inspector Xiao Ang beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He joined a Wei defector, Du Jing, in a plot against the prefectural seat; Inspector Xiao Ang executed him.

sentences.zh: 曹景宗

translations.literal: Cao Jingzong
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzong

sentences.zh: 曹景宗字子震，新野人也。

translations.literal: Cao Jingzong, styled Zizhen, was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzong, courtesy name Zizhen, was from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 父欣之，仕宋位徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xinzhi served Song as Xuzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinzhi had served the Song as inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 景宗幼善騎射，好畋獵，常與少年數十人澤中逐獐鹿，每眾騎赴鹿，鹿馬相亂，景宗於眾中射之，人皆懼中馬足，鹿應弦輒斃，以此為樂。

translations.literal: Jingzong in youth was skilled at riding and shooting and loved hunting; he often with several dozen youths chased roebuck and deer in the marshes; whenever the mass of riders rushed the deer, deer and horses mingled in confusion, and Jingzong shot among them—everyone feared hitting a horse's leg, yet the deer at each bowshot fell dead; he took this as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he excelled at horsemanship and archery and loved the hunt, often chasing deer in the marshes with dozens of companions; when riders and deer tangled, he shot into the press while others feared striking a horse—yet every arrow dropped a deer, which delighted him.

sentences.zh: 未弱冠，欣之於新野遣出州，以匹馬將數人，于中路卒逢蠻賊數百圍之。

translations.literal: Before the capping age, Xinzhi at Xinye sent him out of the province with one horse and a few men; on the road he suddenly met several hundred Man bandits surrounding them.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age his father sent him from Xinye with a single horse and a handful of men; midway several hundred Man raiders surrounded them.

sentences.zh: 景宗帶百餘箭，每箭殺蠻，蠻遂散走。

translations.literal: Jingzong carried over a hundred arrows; each arrow killed a Man, and the Man scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He had more than a hundred arrows; each flight killed a raider until they broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 因以膽勇聞。

translations.literal: Thus his bold courage became known.
translations.idiomatic: His courage became famous from this.

sentences.zh: 頗愛史書，每讀穰苴、樂毅傳，輒放卷歎息曰：「丈夫當如是！」

translations.literal: He rather loved historical books; whenever he read the biographies of Rang Ju and Yue Yi he would lay aside the scroll and sigh, "A man should be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: He loved history; reading the lives of Rang Ju and Yue Yi he would close the book and sigh, "A man should be like that!"

sentences.zh: 少與州里張道門善，道門，車騎將軍敬兒少子也，為武陵太守。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with fellow townsman Zhang Daomen; Daomen, youngest son of Chariots-and-Cavalry General Jing'er, was Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he befriended Zhang Daomen of his district—Daomen, youngest son of General Jing'er, was prefect of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 敬兒誅，道門於郡伏法，親屬故吏莫敢收。

translations.literal: When Jing'er was executed, Daomen was put to death in the commandery; kin and former subordinates dared not collect the body.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing'er was killed, Daomen was executed in his commandery and none of kin or old staff dared recover the corpse.

sentences.zh: 景宗自襄陽遣船到武陵，收其屍，迎還殯葬。

translations.literal: Jingzong from Xiangyang sent a boat to Wuling, collected the corpse, and brought it back for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong sent a boat from Xiangyang, recovered the body, and buried him at home.

sentences.zh: 鄉里以此義之。

translations.literal: The countryside for this held him righteous.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors praised him for the act.

sentences.zh: 仕齊以軍功累加遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, through military merit he was repeatedly advanced to General of Mobile Strikes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he rose by battle merit to general of mobile strikes.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，隨太尉陳顯達北圍馬圈，以奇兵二千破魏援中山王英四萬人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu, following Grand Marshal Chen Xianda north to besiege Maquan, with two thousand picked troops he broke the Wei relief force of Prince of Zhongshan Ying—forty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year four he followed Grand Marshal Chen Xianda to besiege Maquan and with two thousand elite troops shattered Prince Ying of Zhongshan's forty-thousand-man relief column.

sentences.zh: 及克馬圈，顯達論功，以景宗為後。

translations.literal: When Maquan was taken, Xianda assessed merit and ranked Jingzong last.
translations.idiomatic: When Maquan fell, Xianda ranked merits and placed Jingzong last.

sentences.zh: 景宗退無怨言。

translations.literal: Jingzong withdrew without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong withdrew without a word of grievance.

sentences.zh: 魏孝文率眾大至，顯達宵奔，景宗導入山道，故顯達父子獲全。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei led a great host; Xianda fled by night; Jingzong guided him into mountain paths, so Xianda father and son were preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen of Wei came in force, Xianda fled by night; Jingzong led him on mountain paths and father and son escaped whole.

sentences.zh: 梁武為雍州刺史，景宗深自結附，數請帝臨其宅。

translations.literal: When Liang Wudi was Inspector of Yongzhou, Jingzong deeply attached himself and repeatedly invited the Emperor to his house.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi was inspector of Yongzhou, Jingzong courted him closely and often asked him to his home.

sentences.zh: 時天下方亂，帝亦厚加意焉，表為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: The realm was then in turmoil and the Emperor also treated him generously, memorializing him Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire in chaos Wudi favored him and had him named prefect of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 及帝起兵，景宗聚眾並率五服內子弟三百人從軍，遣親人杜思沖勸先迎南康王於襄陽即位，武帝不從。

translations.literal: When the Emperor raised arms, Jingzong gathered troops and led three hundred kinsmen within five degrees of mourning to follow the army, sending his kinsman Du Sichong to urge first welcoming the Prince of Nankang at Xiangyang to ascend—Wudi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi rose in arms, Jingzong mustered troops and led three hundred close kin into the host; he sent Du Sichong to urge enthroning the Prince of Nankang at Xiangyang first—Wudi refused.

sentences.zh: 及至竟陵，以景宗為軍鋒。

translations.literal: On reaching Jingling he was made army point.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Jingling, he was made the army's spearhead.

sentences.zh: 道次江寧，東昏將李居士以重兵鎮新亭，景宗被甲馳戰，居士棄甲奔走，景宗皆獲之。

translations.literal: Passing Jiangning, Dong Hun's general Li Jushi held Xinting with a heavy force; Jingzong armored and galloped to battle; Jushi cast off armor and fled; Jingzong captured all.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangning, Dong Hun's Li Jushi held Xinting with a strong garrison; Jingzong charged in armor, Jushi fled stripped of armor, and Jingzong took all.

sentences.zh: 又與王茂、呂僧珍掎角，破王珍國於大航。

translations.literal: He also with Wang Mao and Lü Sengzhen attacked from two sides and broke Wang Zhenguo at Dahang.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Mao and Lü Sengzhen he took Wang Zhenguo at Dahang in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 景宗軍士皆桀黠無賴，御道左右莫非富室，抄掠財物，略奪子女，景宗不能禁。

translations.literal: Jingzong's soldiers were all fierce and ungoverned; along the imperial avenue none were not rich houses—they plundered goods and seized sons and daughters; Jingzong could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were unruly ruffians; along the imperial way every house was wealthy—they looted goods and seized women, and he could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 及武帝入頓西城，嚴申號令，然後稍息。

translations.literal: When the Emperor entered and encamped at West City, he strictly proclaimed orders, and then it gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Wudi encamped at West City and enforced stern orders did the pillage ease.

sentences.zh: 城平，封湘西縣侯，除郢州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When the city was pacified he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangxi County, appointed Inspector of Yingzhou, with overall command added.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell he was made Marquis of Xiangxi, inspector of Yingzhou, with overall command.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，改封竟陵縣侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was changed to Marquis of Jingling County.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year one his marquisate was changed to Jingling.

sentences.zh: 景宗在州，鬻貨聚斂，于城南起宅，長堤以東，夏口以北，開街列門，東西數里。

translations.literal: Jingzong in the province sold goods and amassed wealth; south of the city he raised a mansion—from the long embankment east to north of Xiakou he opened streets and gates, several li east and west.
translations.idiomatic: In office he traded and hoarded wealth and south of the city built a mansion stretching from the long dike east to north of Xiakou, streets and gates for li in every direction.

sentences.zh: 而部曲殘橫，人頗厭之。

translations.literal: Yet his retainers were brutal and overbearing, and people greatly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: His household troops were violent, and the people loathed him.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，魏攻司州，圍刺史蔡道恭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year Wei attacked Sizhou and besieged Inspector Cai Daogong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year two Wei attacked Sizhou and besieged Inspector Cai Daogong.

sentences.zh: 城中負板而汲，景宗望關門不出，但耀軍遊獵而已。

translations.literal: In the city they carried boards to draw water; Jingzong watched the pass gate and did not go out, only displaying the army on hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders carried planks to draw water under fire; Jingzong stayed at the pass gate, parading his host on hunts rather than relieving the siege.

sentences.zh: 及司州城陷，為御史中丞任昉所奏。

translations.literal: When Sizhou city fell he was memorialized by Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sizhou fell, Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝以功臣不問，徵為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor, as he was a merit minister, did not inquire and summoned him as Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi, honoring his founding merit, did not punish him and summoned him as right guard general.

sentences.zh: 五年，魏中山王英攻鍾離，圍徐州刺史昌義之，武帝詔景宗督眾軍援義之，豫州刺史韋叡亦援焉，而受景宗節度。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Prince Ying of Zhongshan of Wei attacked Zhongli and besieged Xuzhou Inspector Chang Yizhi; Wudi ordered Jingzong to command the host to rescue Yizhi; Yuzhou Inspector Wei Rui also aided, yet under Jingzong's command.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Prince Ying of Zhongshan besieged Zhongli and trapped Xuzhou inspector Chang Yizhi; Wudi ordered Jingzong to command all forces to relieve him, with Yuzhou inspector Wei Rui also under his command.

sentences.zh: 詔景宗頓道人洲，待眾軍齊集俱進。

translations.literal: Edict ordered Jingzong to encamp at Daoren Isle and wait until the hosts were all gathered to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had him halt at Daoren Isle until every column assembled.

sentences.zh: 景宗欲專其功，乃違敕而進，遇暴風卒起，頗有沈溺，復還守先頓。

translations.literal: Jingzong wished to monopolize the merit and therefore disobeyed the edict and advanced; he met a sudden violent wind, many drowned, and he returned to hold the former camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wanting the glory alone, he disobeyed and advanced; a sudden gale sank many boats and he fell back to his old camp.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之曰：「此所以破賊也。

translations.literal: The Emperor on hearing said, "This is how the bandits are broken.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Wudi said, "This is how the enemy will be broken.

sentences.zh: 景宗不進，蓋天意乎。

translations.literal: Jingzong not advancing—was it perhaps Heaven's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Had Jingzong pressed on alone, would it not have been Heaven's will that he hold back?

sentences.zh: 若孤軍獨往，城不時立，必見狼狽。

translations.literal: If he marched alone, the city would not be taken in time, and he would surely be thrown into distress.
translations.idiomatic: Had he pushed on alone, the city might not have fallen in time and his force would have been thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 今得待眾軍同進，始可大捷矣。」

translations.literal: Now we can wait for the hosts to advance together—then a great victory may be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Now, waiting for the whole army to advance together, a great victory was still possible.

sentences.zh: 及韋叡至，與景宗進頓邵陽洲，立壘與魏城相去百餘步。

translations.literal: When Wei Rui arrived, he and Jingzong advanced to encamp at Shaoyang Isle and built ramparts a hundred-odd paces from the Wei city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Rui came up, he and Jingzong moved to Shaoyang Isle and threw up works barely a hundred paces from the Wei lines.

sentences.zh: 魏連戰不能卻，傷殺者十二三，自是魏軍不敢逼。

translations.literal: Wei fought repeatedly but could not drive them back; casualties were twelve or thirteen in ten—thereafter the Wei army did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated Wei assaults failed; they lost perhaps two or three men in ten, and thereafter dared not close.

sentences.zh: 景宗等器甲精新，魏人望而奪氣。

translations.literal: Jingzong and the others had fresh, fine armor and weapons; the Wei men looked on and lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Their gear was bright and new; the Wei troops looked on and their courage failed.

sentences.zh: 魏將楊大眼對橋北岸立城，以通糧運。

translations.literal: Wei general Yang Dayan built a city on the north bank of the bridge to keep grain transport open.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei commander Yang Dayan fortified the north bank of the bridge to keep supplies moving.

sentences.zh: 每牧人過岸伐芻藳，皆為大眼所略。

translations.literal: Whenever herders crossed the river to cut fodder, Dayan seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever drovers crossed to cut fodder, Dayan took them.

sentences.zh: 景宗乃募勇敢士千餘人，徑度大眼城南數里築壘，親自舉築。

translations.literal: Jingzong therefore recruited over a thousand brave men, crossed several li south of Dayan's city, and built a rampart, himself raising the earthwork.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong raised a thousand bold men, crossed south of Dayan's walls by several li, and built a fort, working the rampart himself.

sentences.zh: 大眼來攻，景宗破之，因得壘成。

translations.literal: Dayan came to attack; Jingzong defeated him and thus completed the rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan attacked; Jingzong beat him off and finished the work.

sentences.zh: 使別將趙草守之，因謂為趙草城。

translations.literal: He sent a separate commander Zhao Cao to hold it, and therefore called it Zhao Cao Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He left Zhao Cao to hold it, and men called it Zhao Cao Fort.

sentences.zh: 是後恣芻牧馬。

translations.literal: Thereafter they grazed horses and cut fodder at will.
translations.idiomatic: After that they grazed and cut fodder freely.

sentences.zh: 大眼遣抄掠，輒為趙草所獲。

translations.literal: When Dayan sent raiders, Zhao Cao always captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan's raiders were always taken by Zhao Cao.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔景宗等預裝高艦，使與魏橋等，為火攻計。

translations.literal: Earlier, edict had ordered Jingzong and the others to prepare tall warships in advance, to match the Wei bridges for a fire attack plan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier they had been ordered to ready tall ships to match the Wei bridges for a fire attack.

sentences.zh: 令景宗與叡各攻一橋。

translations.literal: They ordered Jingzong and Rui each to assault one bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong and Rui were each to take one bridge.

sentences.zh: 叡攻其南，景宗攻其北。

translations.literal: Rui attacked the south; Jingzong the north.
translations.idiomatic: Rui struck the south span; Jingzong the north.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，因春水生，淮水暴長六七尺。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, because spring waters rose, the Huai surged six or seven chi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year six the spring floods raised the Huai six or seven feet.

sentences.zh: 叡遣所督將馮道根、李文釗、裴邃、韋寂等乘艦登岸，擊魏洲上軍盡殪。

translations.literal: Rui sent his commanders Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji, and others to board ships and land, striking the Wei troops on the isle and slaughtering them all.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's columns—Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji—landed from the ships and wiped out the Wei force on the isle.

sentences.zh: 景宗使眾軍復鼓噪亂登諸城，呼聲震天地，大眼於西岸燒營，英自東岸棄城走，諸壘相次土崩，悉棄其器甲，爭投水死，淮水為之不流。

translations.literal: Jingzong made the host drum and storm the walls; the clamor shook heaven and earth; Dayan burned his camp on the west bank, Ying abandoned the east city and fled; the forts collapsed in succession; they cast off armor and weapons and threw themselves into the water to die—the Huai ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong's men stormed the walls with thunderous drums; Dayan burned his west-bank camp, Ying fled east, fort after fort gave way, and the enemy cast off armor and drowned until the Huai seemed to stand still.

sentences.zh: 景宗命軍主馬廣躡大眼至濊水上四十餘里，伏屍相枕。

translations.literal: Jingzong ordered Army Commander Ma Guang to pursue Dayan more than forty li to the Huishui; corpses lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ma Guang after Dayan more than forty li to the Huishui, corpses heaped along the way.

sentences.zh: 義之出逐英至洛口，英以匹馬入梁城，緣淮百餘里屍骸相藉。

translations.literal: Yizhi pursued Ying to Luokou; Ying entered Liang city on one horse; along the Huai for a hundred-odd li corpses lay piled.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi chased Ying to Luokou; Ying entered Liang city on a single horse; for a hundred li along the Huai the dead lay in heaps.

sentences.zh: 虜五萬餘人，收其軍糧器械山積，牛馬驢騾不可稱計。

translations.literal: Captives exceeded fifty thousand; captured grain, weapons, and gear piled like mountains; cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than fifty thousand captives, mountains of grain and arms, and beasts of burden beyond count.

sentences.zh: 景宗乃搜所得生口萬餘人，馬千匹，遣獻捷。

translations.literal: Jingzong then searched out over ten thousand living captives and a thousand horses and sent them to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong gathered ten thousand prisoners and a thousand horses and sent word of victory.

sentences.zh: 先是旱甚，詔祈蔣帝神求雨，十旬不降。

translations.literal: Earlier the drought had been severe; edict ordered prayers to the god of Jiangdi for rain—ten ten-day periods passed without rain.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought had led the court to pray at Jiangdi for rain; ten weeks passed dry.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命載荻欲焚蔣廟並神影。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and ordered reeds loaded to burn Jiang Temple and the god's image.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi in anger ordered reeds to burn the temple and the god's image.

sentences.zh: 爾日開朗，欲起火，當神上忽有雲如傘，倏忽驟雨如寫，台中宮殿皆自振動。

translations.literal: That day it cleared; just as fire was to be set, suddenly above the god a cloud like an umbrella; rain poured in torrents; palace halls in the capital all trembled.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky cleared; as fire was kindled a canopy-like cloud appeared and rain fell in sheets; the palace buildings shook.

sentences.zh: 帝懼，馳詔追停，少時還靜。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared it, galloped edict to stop, and shortly all was calm again.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi in fear sent orders to stop; soon all was still.

sentences.zh: 自此帝畏信遂深。

translations.literal: From then his fearful faith grew deep.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter his faith in the god deepened.

sentences.zh: 自踐阼以來，未嘗躬自到廟，於是備法駕將朝臣修謁。

translations.literal: Since his accession he had never personally visited the temple; now he prepared the full imperial train with court ministers to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne he had never visited in person; now he went in state with his ministers.

sentences.zh: 是時，魏軍攻圍鍾離，蔣帝神報敕，必許扶助。

translations.literal: At that time Wei was besieging Zhongli; the god of Jiangdi reported in a revelation that aid was promised.
translations.idiomatic: While Wei besieged Zhongli, the god promised aid in a revelation.

sentences.zh: 既而無雨水長，遂挫敵人，亦神之力焉。

translations.literal: Shortly after, without rain the waters rose and the enemy was checked—also the god's power.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the waters rose without rain and the enemy was broken—again the god's doing.

sentences.zh: 凱旋之後，廟中人馬腳盡有泥濕，當時並目睹焉。

translations.literal: After the triumphal return, men and horses in the temple all had wet, muddy feet—many saw it at the time.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory, men and horses in the temple bore wet, muddy hooves—witnesses saw it.

sentences.zh: 景宗振旅凱入，帝于華光殿宴飲連句，令左僕射沈約賦韻。

translations.literal: Jingzong led the triumphant host in; the Emperor at Hualight Hall feasted with linked verses and ordered Left Vice Director Shen Yue to assign rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong marched home in triumph; Wudi feasted at Hualight Hall in linked verse and set Shen Yue to assign rhymes.

sentences.zh: 景宗不得韻，意色不平，啟求賦詩。

translations.literal: Jingzong could not match the rhyme; his expression was displeased; he memorialized asking to compose a poem.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong drew no rhyme and looked sour; he asked to improvise a poem.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿伎能甚多，人才英拔，何必止在一詩。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Your skills are many and your talent outstanding—why limit yourself to one poem?
translations.idiomatic: Wudi said, "Your talents are many—why insist on one poem?

sentences.zh: 景宗已醉，求作不已，詔令約賦韻。

translations.literal: Jingzong was already drunk and pressed on; edict ordered Yue to assign rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he pressed on until Yue was told to fix a rhyme.

sentences.zh: 時韻已盡，唯餘競病二字。

translations.literal: The rhymes were exhausted; only "compete" and "sickness" remained.
translations.idiomatic: All rhymes were used; only jing (compete) and bing (sickness) were left.

sentences.zh: 景宗便操筆，斯須而成，其辭曰：「去時兒女悲，歸來笳鼓競。

translations.literal: Jingzong took up the brush and in a moment finished; the words said, "When I went, sons and daughters wept; returning, pipes and drums compete.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the brush and at once wrote, "When I went, my children wept; returning, pipes and drums compete.

sentences.zh: 借問行路人，何如霍去病。」

translations.literal: I ask travelers on the road—how do I compare to Huo Qubing?"
translations.idiomatic: I ask passersby—how do I compare to Huo Qubing?

sentences.zh: 帝歎不已。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed without end.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi sighed with unending admiration.

sentences.zh: 約及朝賢驚嗟竟日，詔令上左史。

translations.literal: Yue and court worthies marveled all day; edict ordered it entered in the Left Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue and the court marveled all day; the poem was entered in the Left Historian.

sentences.zh: 於是進爵為公，拜侍中、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was advanced to duke and made Palace Attendant and General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to duke, made palace attendant, and general who leads the army.

sentences.zh: 景宗為人自恃尚勝，每作書字，有不解，不以問人，皆以意造，雖公卿無所推；

translations.literal: Jingzong was by nature self-reliant and fond of outdoing others; whenever he wrote characters he did not understand he would not ask others but invent by intent—even toward grandees he would not defer.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and competitive, he would not ask when a character baffled him but guessed at it, deferring even to grandees.

sentences.zh: 唯以韋叡年長，且州里勝流，特相敬重，同宴御筵，亦曲躬謙遜。

translations.literal: Only toward Wei Rui, who was older and a leading man of the province, did he especially respect him; at the same imperial feast he still bowed with humble courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wei Rui, older and a leading man of their province, won his deep respect—at imperial feasts he still bowed with humble courtesy.

sentences.zh: 武帝以此嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 景宗好內，妓妾至數百，窮極錦繡。

translations.literal: Jingzong loved women; concubines and entertainers reached several hundred, with brocade and embroidery pushed to excess.
translations.idiomatic: He loved women; concubines and entertainers numbered in the hundreds, with brocade pushed to excess.

sentences.zh: 性躁動，不能沈默。

translations.literal: His nature was restless and he could not be still.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was restless; he could not be still.

sentences.zh: 出行常欲褰車帷幔，左右輒諫以位望隆重，人所具瞻，不宜然。

translations.literal: Going out he always wished to lift the carriage curtains; attendants would admonish that with his rank and dignity men looked to him—it was not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Going out he always wished to raise the carriage curtains; attendants admonished that with his rank and dignity all eyes were on him—it was not fitting.

sentences.zh: 景宗謂所親曰：「我昔在鄉里，騎快馬如龍，與年少輩數十騎，拓弓弦作礔靂聲，箭如餓鴟叫，平澤中逐獐，數肋射之，渴飲其血，饑食其脯，甜如甘露漿。

translations.literal: Jingzong told those close to him, "In the old days in the countryside I rode a swift horse like a dragon with several dozen youths; drawing the bowstring sounded like thunder, arrows like hungry owls crying; in the open marsh we chased roe deer, shooting several ribs at a run, drinking their blood when thirsty, eating their flesh when hungry—sweet as sweet dew.
translations.idiomatic: He told those close to him, "Once in the countryside I rode a swift horse like a dragon with dozens of youths; the bowstring cracked like thunder, arrows cried like hungry owls; in the open marsh we chased roe deer, shot several ribs at a run, drank their blood when thirsty, ate their flesh when hungry—sweet as dew.

sentences.zh: 覺耳後生風，鼻頭出火，此樂使人忘死，不知老之將至。

translations.literal: I felt wind behind my ears and fire at my nostrils; such joy makes one forget death and not know old age draws near.
translations.idiomatic: Wind whistled behind my ears and fire seemed to burst from my nostrils; such joy makes one forget death and not know age is coming.

sentences.zh: 今來揚州作貴人，動轉不得。

translations.literal: Now coming to Yangzhou as a noble, I can hardly move.
translations.idiomatic: Now in Yangzhou as a noble I can hardly stir.

sentences.zh: 路行開車幔，小人輒言不可。

translations.literal: On the road I open the carriage curtain and petty men say it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: On the road I raise the curtain and petty men say it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 閉置車中，如三日新婦，此邑邑使人氣盡。」

translations.literal: Shut in the carriage like a bride of three days—this suffocates a man."
translations.idiomatic: Shut in the carriage like a bride of three days—this suffocates the spirit.

sentences.zh: 為人嗜酒好樂，臘月於宅中使人作邪呼逐除，遍往人家乞酒食。

translations.literal: He was fond of wine and music; in the twelfth month at his house he had men perform demon-shouts and expulsion rites, going from house to house begging food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and music; in the twelfth month he had men perform demon-shouts and expulsion rites, going house to house begging food and drink.

sentences.zh: 本以為戲，而部下多剽輕，因弄人婦女，奪人財貨。

translations.literal: It was meant as play, but many of his subordinates were violent; they molested women and seized goods.
translations.idiomatic: It was meant as play, but many subordinates were violent; they molested women and seized goods.

sentences.zh: 帝頗知之，景宗懼乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew something of it; Jingzong in fear then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor learned of it; Jingzong in fear then stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝數宴見功臣，共道故舊。

translations.literal: The Emperor often feasted the merit ministers and together recalled old days.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often feasted the merit ministers and together recalled old days.

sentences.zh: 景宗酒後謬妄，或誤稱下官。

translations.literal: After wine Jingzong would speak wildly or mistakenly call himself "your subordinate."
translations.idiomatic: After wine Jingzong would speak wildly or mistakenly call himself "your subordinate."

sentences.zh: 帝故縱之，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: The Emperor deliberately indulged him and took it as laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor deliberately indulged him and took it as laughter.

sentences.zh: 後為江州刺史，赴任卒於道。

translations.literal: Later he was Jiangzhou Inspector and died on the way to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Jiangzhou Inspector and died on the way to his post.

sentences.zh: 贈雍州刺史、開府儀同三司，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously Yongzhou Inspector, equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies with an opening office; posthumous title Strong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Yongzhou Inspector, with Three Excellency ceremony and an opening office; posthumous title Strong.

sentences.zh: 子皎嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jiao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 景宗齊永元初任竟陵郡，其第九弟義宗年少，未有位宦，居在雍州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan of Qi, Jingzong held Jingling commandery; his ninth younger brother Yizong was young and without office, dwelling in Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan of Qi, Jingzong held Jingling commandery; his ninth younger brother Yizong was young and without office, dwelling in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 既方伯之弟，又是豪強之門。

translations.literal: As a prefect's brother and a powerful house at the market edge.
translations.idiomatic: As a prefect's brother and a powerful house at the market edge.

sentences.zh: 市邊富人姓向以見錢百萬欲埤義宗，以妹適之。

translations.literal: A rich man of the market surnamed Xiang, seeing cash of a million, wished to betroth Yizong and give his sister.
translations.idiomatic: A rich man of the market surnamed Xiang, seeing cash of a million, wished to betroth Yizong and give his sister.

sentences.zh: 義宗遣人送書竟陵諮景宗，景宗題書後答曰：「買猶未得，云何已賣。」

translations.literal: Yizong sent word to Jingzong at Jingling for advice; Jingzong wrote on the letter and replied, "Buying is not yet done—how can you already sell?
translations.idiomatic: Yizong sent word to Jingzong at Jingling for advice; Jingzong wrote on the letter and replied, "Buying is not yet done—how can you already sell?

sentences.zh: 義宗貪鏹遂成。

translations.literal: Yizong, greedy for cash, completed the match.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong, greedy for cash, completed the match.

sentences.zh: 後隨武帝西下，歷位梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Emperor west; he successively held Liang and Qin as Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed the Emperor west; he successively held Liang and Qin as inspector.

sentences.zh: 向家兄弟憑附曹氏，位登列卿。

translations.literal: The Xiang brothers relied on the Cao clan and rose to ranked ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiang brothers relied on the Cao clan and rose to ranked ministers.

sentences.zh: 後義宗為都督，征穰城，軍敗，見獲于魏，卒。

translations.literal: Later Yizong was overall commander, campaigned against Xiangcheng, the army was defeated, was captured by Wei, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yizong was overall commander, campaigned against Xiangcheng, the army was defeated, was captured by Wei, and died.

sentences.zh: 席闡文

translations.literal: Xi Chanwen
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chanwen

sentences.zh: 席闡文，安定臨涇人也。

translations.literal: Xi Chanwen was a native of Linjing in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chanwen was a native of Linjing in Anding.

sentences.zh: 孤貧，涉獵書史。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor, he ranged through books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he ranged through books and histories.

sentences.zh: 齊初，為雍州刺史蕭赤斧中兵參軍，由是與其子穎胄善。

translations.literal: In early Qi he was Central Army Commander under Yongzhou Inspector Xiao Chifu, and through this became friendly with his son Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In early Qi he was central army commander under Yongzhou Inspector Xiao Chifu, and through this became friendly with his son Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 復曆西中郎中兵參軍，領城局。

translations.literal: He again served as Western Central Commandant Army Commander, in charge of the city bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Western Central Commandant army commander, in charge of the city bureau.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝之將起兵，闡文勸穎胄同焉，仍遣客田祖恭私報帝，並獻銀裝刀，帝報以金如意。

translations.literal: When Liang Wudi was about to raise arms, Chanwen urged Yingzhou to join and sent his client Tian Zugong in secret to report to the Emperor and present a silver-mounted knife; the Emperor returned a gold ruyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Wudi was about to raise arms, Chanwen urged Yingzhou to join and sent his client Tian Zugong in secret to report to the Emperor and present a silver-mounted knife; the Emperor returned a gold ruyi.

sentences.zh: 和帝稱尊號，為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor He was honored with the exalted title, he was made Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He was honored with the exalted title, he was made Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 穎胄暴卒，州府騷擾，闡文以和帝幼弱，中流任重，時始興王憺留鎮雍部，乃與西朝群臣迎憺總州事，故賴以寧輯。

translations.literal: When Yingzhou died suddenly, the province and prefecture were disturbed; Chanwen, because Emperor He was young and the midstream task weighty, and the Prince of Shixing Dan was then guarding Yong, together with western court ministers welcomed Dan to oversee provincial affairs—thus they relied on him for calm.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzhou died suddenly, the province and prefecture were disturbed; Chanwen, because Emperor He was young and the midstream task weighty, and the Prince of Shixing Dan was then guarding Yong, together with western court ministers welcomed Dan to oversee provincial affairs—thus they relied on him for calm.

sentences.zh: 帝受禪，除都官尚書，封山陽伯，出為東陽太守。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the Mandate, he was made Minister of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed Baron of Shanyang, and sent out as Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor received the Mandate, he was made Minister of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed Baron of Shanyang, and sent out as Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 在郡有能名。

translations.literal: In the commandery he had a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he had a name for ability.

sentences.zh: 冬至，悉放獄中囚，依期而至。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice he released all prisoners in the jail; they returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice he released all prisoners in the jail; they returned on schedule.

sentences.zh: 改封湘西侯。

translations.literal: Changed enfeoffment to Marquis of Xiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Changed enfeoffment to Marquis of Xiangxi.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous title Majestic.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; posthumous title Majestic.

sentences.zh: 夏侯詳

translations.literal: Xiahou Xiang
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xiang

sentences.zh: 夏侯詳字叔業，譙郡譙人也。

translations.literal: Xiahou Xiang, styled Shuye, was a native of Qiao in Qiao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xiang, styled Shuye, was a native of Qiao in Qiao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 年十六遭父艱，居喪哀毀，三年廬於墓側。

translations.literal: At sixteen he suffered his father's death; in mourning he was so grief-stricken he dwelt three years in a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he suffered his father's death; in mourning he was so grief-stricken he dwelt three years in a hut beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 嘗有三足雀來集其廬戶，眾咸異焉。

translations.literal: Once a three-legged sparrow came to perch on his hut door; all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Once a three-legged sparrow came to perch on his hut door; all regarded it as strange.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為新汲令，政有異績。

translations.literal: Serving Song as Magistrate of Xinzuo, his administration had unusual results.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Song as Magistrate of Xinzuo, his administration had unusual results.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史段佛榮班下境內，為屬城表。

translations.literal: Yuzhou Inspector Duan Furong toured the territory within his borders; as a subordinate city he was memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou Inspector Duan Furong toured the territory within his borders; as a subordinate city he was memorialized.

sentences.zh: 轉中從事史，仍遷別駕。

translations.literal: Moved to Central Attendant Officer, then promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Central Attendant Officer, then promoted to Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 曆事八將，州部稱之。

translations.literal: He served eight generals and the province and commandery praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He served eight generals and the province and commandery praised him.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝為刺史，雅相器遇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Qi was inspector, he greatly valued and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Qi was inspector, he greatly valued and favored him.

sentences.zh: 及輔政，引詳及裴叔業日夜與語，詳輒不酬。

translations.literal: When he aided the government, he drew Xiang and Pei Shuye to speak with day and night; Xiang would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When he aided the government, he drew Xiang and Pei Shuye to speak with day and night; Xiang would not respond.

sentences.zh: 帝以問叔業，叔業以告詳。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Shuye; Shuye told Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Shuye; Shuye told Xiang.

sentences.zh: 詳曰：「不為福始，不為禍先。」

translations.literal: Xiang said, "Do not be the start of fortune, do not be the start of calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Do not be the start of fortune, do not be the start of calamity.

sentences.zh: 由此微有忤。

translations.literal: From this he was slightly at odds.
translations.idiomatic: From this he was slightly at odds.

sentences.zh: 出為征虜長史、義陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief of Staff to the Expeditionary Army and Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Chief of Staff to the Expeditionary Army and Administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 及南康王為荊州，詳為西中郎司馬、新興太守。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nankang was in Jingzhou, Xiang was Western Central Commandant Marshal and Administrator of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Nankang was in Jingzhou, Xiang was Western Central Commandant Marshal and Administrator of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝起兵，長史蕭穎胄同創大舉，慮詳不同，以告柳忱。

translations.literal: When Liang Wudi raised arms, Chief Administrator Xiao Yingzhou joined the great enterprise; fearing Xiang would not agree, he told Liu Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Wudi raised arms, Chief Administrator Xiao Yingzhou joined the great enterprise; fearing Xiang would not agree, he told Liu Chen.

sentences.zh: 忱曰：「易耳。

translations.literal: Chen said, "That is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "That is easy.

sentences.zh: 近詳求昏未之許，令成昏而告之，不憂立異。」

translations.literal: Xiang recently sought marriage and I did not yet consent; let the marriage be concluded and then tell him—no fear he will stand apart."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang recently sought marriage and I did not yet consent; let the marriage be concluded and then tell him—no fear he will stand apart."

sentences.zh: 於是以女適其子夔。

translations.literal: He therefore gave his daughter to Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore gave his daughter to Kui.

sentences.zh: 大事方建，西台以詳為中領軍，加散騎常侍、南郡太守。

translations.literal: As the great affair was being founded, the western court made Xiang Central Army Commander, with added Palace Cadet and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: As the great enterprise took shape, the western court made Xiang central army commander with Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 凡軍國大事，穎胄多決於詳。

translations.literal: In military and state affairs great and small, Yingzhou mostly decided through Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: On military and civil matters, Yingzhou mostly followed Xiang.

sentences.zh: 頃之穎胄卒，梁武弟始興王憺留守襄陽，詳乃遣使迎憺共參軍國。

translations.literal: Shortly Yingzhou died; Liang Wudi's younger brother the Prince of Shixing Dan was guarding Xiangyang; Xiang then sent envoys to welcome Dan to join in overseeing military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yingzhou died; Xiang brought Prince Dan of Shixing from Xiangyang to steady army and state.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、尚書右僕射，尋授荊州刺史，詳又固讓於憺。

translations.literal: Moved to Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; soon appointed Jingzhou Inspector—Xiang again firmly declined in favor of Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He became palace attendant and right vice director, then inspector of Jingzhou, but again yielded to Dan.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，徵為侍中、車騎將軍，封甯都縣侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was summoned as Palace Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry, enfeoffed Marquis of Ningdu County.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year one he was summoned as palace attendant and general of chariots and cavalry, Marquis of Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 詳累讓，乃更授右光祿大夫，侍中如故，給親信二十人，改封豐城縣公。

translations.literal: Xiang repeatedly declined and was instead made Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Palace Attendant as before, twenty personal attendants, changed to Duke of Fengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He declined until made right grand master of splendid happiness, still palace attendant, with twenty attendants, then Duke of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was moved to Xiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he went to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詳善吏事，在州四載，為百姓所稱。

translations.literal: Xiang was skilled in administration; four years in the province the common people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in administration, in four years the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 州城南臨水有峻峰，舊傳云：「刺史登此山輒代」，由是曆政莫敢至，詳於其地起台榭，延僚屬，以表損挹之志。

translations.literal: South of the provincial city the waters faced a steep peak; old tradition said, "When an inspector climbs this mountain he is replaced," so for generations none in office dared go; Xiang on that ground raised terraces and pavilions and entertained subordinates to show his modest intent.
translations.idiomatic: A peak south of the city was said to doom any inspector who climbed it; Xiang built halls there anyway to show he did not fear the omen.

sentences.zh: 後徵為尚書左僕射、金紫光祿大夫，道病卒。

translations.literal: Later summoned as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal; he died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as left vice director, he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 上為素服舉哀，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰景。

translations.literal: The Emperor wore plain robes and raised mourning; posthumously equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies with an opening office; posthumous title Bright.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi mourned in plain dress and posthumously gave him Three Excellency ceremony; posthumous name Bright.

sentences.zh: 子亶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dan inherited.

sentences.zh: 子 亶

translations.literal: Son Dan
translations.idiomatic: Son Dan

sentences.zh: 亶字世龍，齊永元末，父詳為西中郎南康王司馬，隨府鎮荊州，亶留都下，為東昏聽政主帥。

translations.literal: Dan, styled Shilong—in the last year of Yongyuan of Qi his father Xiang was Western Central Commandant Marshal to the Prince of Nankang, following the prefecture to guard Jingzhou; Dan remained in the capital as commandant of Donghun's audience office.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, courtesy name Shilong, stayed in the capital while his father guarded Jingzhou with the Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 及崔慧景作亂，亶以捍禦功，除驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing rebelled, Dan for defending merit was made General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing rebelled, Dan's defense won him general of valiant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及梁武起兵，詳與長史蕭穎胄協同，密遣迎亶。

translations.literal: When Liang Wudi raised arms, Xiang and Chief Administrator Yingzhou joined together and secretly sent to welcome Dan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi rose, Xiang and Yingzhou secretly summoned Dan.

sentences.zh: 亶乃齎宣德皇后令，令南康王纂承大統。

translations.literal: Dan then carried Empress Dowager Xuande's order directing the Prince of Nankang to succeed to the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: Dan bore Empress Dowager Xuande's order for the Prince of Nankang to succeed.

sentences.zh: 建鄴平，以亶為尚書吏部郎，俄遷侍中，奉璽於帝。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Dan was made Director of the Ministry of Officials in the Masters of Writing, soon Palace Attendant, bearing the seal to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell he became director of officials, then palace attendant bearing the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 天監六年，累遷南郡太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjian he was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year six he became prefect of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父憂解職，居喪盡禮，廬於墓側，遺財悉推諸弟。

translations.literal: In father's mourning he left office; in mourning he fulfilled all rites, dwelt beside the tomb, and pushed all inherited property to his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he lived by the tomb and gave his inheritance to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 八年，起為司州刺史，領安陸太守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was raised as Inspector of Sizhou, also holding Anlu as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he was inspector of Sizhou and prefect of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 服闋，襲封豐城縣公。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Fengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he inherited Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 居州甚有威惠，為邊人悅服。

translations.literal: In the province he had great authority and kindness; the border people were pleased to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he ruled with authority and kindness; border folk submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 曆都官尚書，遷給事中、右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He successively held Minister of the Imperial Clan and was promoted to Palace Cadet and Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of the imperial clan, then palace cadet and right guard general.

sentences.zh: 累遷吳興太守。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly moved to Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 在郡復有惠政，吏人圖其像，立碑頌美焉。

translations.literal: In the commandery again he had benevolent administration; clerks and people painted his image and raised a stele in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Again his rule won praise; clerks raised a stele with his portrait.

sentences.zh: 普通五年，為中護軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Putong he was Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year five he was central army commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，大舉北侵，先遣豫州刺史裴邃帥譙州刺史湛僧智等自南道攻壽陽，未克而邃卒，乃加亶使持節代邃，與魏將河間王琛、臨淮王彧等相拒，頻戰克捷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year a great northern campaign was launched; first Yuzhou Inspector Pei Sui led Qiao Inspector Zhan Sengzhi and others from the southern route against Shouyang; before it was taken Sui died; Dan was added with staff of authority to replace Sui and resisted Wei generals the Prince of Hejian and the Prince of Linhuai, repeatedly winning.
translations.idiomatic: In year six the great northern campaign sent Pei Sui against Shouyang; when Sui died Dan replaced him and beat Wei princes of Hejian and Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 尋敕班師合肥，須堰成復進。

translations.literal: Soon edict ordered the army to withdraw to Hefei and advance again when the dam was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Edict ordered withdrawal to Hefei until the dam was done.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，淮堰水盛，壽陽城將沒，武帝復遣北道軍元樹帥彭寶孫、陳慶之等稍進。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year the Huai dam's waters swelled and Shouyang's walls were nearly submerged; the Emperor again sent the northern column under Prince Yuan with Peng Baosun and Chen Qingzhi to advance gradually.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven the dam flooded Shouyang; Wudi sent Yuan's column to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 亶帥湛僧智、魚弘、張澄等通清流澗將入淮、肥。

translations.literal: Dan led Zhan Sengzhi, Yu Hong, Zhang Cheng, and others through Qingliu's ravine toward the Huai and Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Dan led columns through Qingliu toward the Huai and Fei.

sentences.zh: 魏軍夾肥築城出亶後，亶與僧智還襲破之。

translations.literal: Wei troops built a city on both sides of Fei behind Dan; Dan and Sengzhi turned and smashed it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei built behind him on the Fei; he turned and broke them.

sentences.zh: 進攻黎漿，貞威將軍韋放自北道會焉。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Lijiang, Valiant Prestige General Wei Fang came from the northern route to join.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Lijiang, Wei Fang joined from the north.

sentences.zh: 兩軍既合，所向皆降，凡降城五十二，獲男女口七萬五千人。

translations.literal: When the two armies joined, wherever they went all surrendered; in all fifty-two cities surrendered, capturing men and women numbering seventy-five thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: United, they took fifty-two cities and seventy-five thousand people.

sentences.zh: 詔以壽陽依前代置豫州，合肥鎮改為南豫州，以亶為豫、南豫二州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Edict placed Shouyang as Yuzhou as in former ages, changed Hefei garrison to South Yuzhou; Dan was made Inspector of Yu and South Yu with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang was made Yuzhou again; Dan held both Yu provinces with overall command.

sentences.zh: 壽春久離兵荒，百姓多流散，亶輕刑薄賦，務農省役，頃之人戶充復。

translations.literal: Shouchun had long lacked soldiers and farming; the people mostly scattered; Dan lightened punishments and taxes, devoted himself to farming and light labor—soon households were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchun, long wasted by war, revived under his light taxes and farming.

sentences.zh: 卒於州鎮。

translations.literal: He died at the provincial garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He died in garrison.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，即日素服舉哀，贈車騎將軍，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: The Emperor on hearing at once wore plain robes and raised mourning; posthumously General of Chariots and Cavalry; posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi mourned in plain dress and made him general of chariots and cavalry posthumously; posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 州人夏侯簡等表請為亶立碑置祠，詔許之。

translations.literal: Provincial men Xiahou Jian and others memorialized to raise a stele and shrine for Dan; edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The province asked for a stele and shrine; Wudi agreed.

sentences.zh: 亶美風儀，寬厚有器量，涉獵文史，能專對。

translations.literal: Dan had fine bearing, was generous and had capacity; he ranged through literature and history and could answer point by point.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome, generous, learned, he could debate any point.

sentences.zh: 宗人夏侯溢為衡陽內史，辭日，亶侍御坐，帝謂亶曰：「夏侯溢於卿疏近？」

translations.literal: Clansman Xiahou Yi was Interior Minister of Hengyang; on the day of his farewell audience Dan attended by the Emperor's seat; the Emperor asked Dan, "Is Xiahou Yi near or distant to you in kin?"
translations.idiomatic: At court Wudi asked whether Inspector Yi was near kin; Dan said he was a cousin."

sentences.zh: 亶答云：「是臣從弟。」

translations.literal: Dan answered, "He is my younger cousin."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "He is my younger cousin."

sentences.zh: 帝知溢於亶已疏，乃曰：「卿傖人，如何不辨族從？」

translations.literal: The Emperor knew Yi was already distant from Dan and said, "You rustic—how can you not distinguish clan kin?"
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yi was distant, Wudi joked, "You rustic—can you not tell kin apart?"

sentences.zh: 亶對曰：「臣聞服屬易疏，所以不忍言族。」

translations.literal: Dan replied, "Your servant has heard that worn-out kinship is easily set aside—therefore I could not bear to speak of clan."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Worn kin is easily cast off—so I would not claim him as clan."

sentences.zh: 時以為能。

translations.literal: At the time this was held ability.
translations.idiomatic: The court admired the wit.

sentences.zh: 亶曆六郡三州，不為產業，祿賜所得，隨散親故。

translations.literal: Dan held six commanderies and three provinces, amassed no property; salary and gifts he scattered to kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Across six commanderies and three provinces he amassed nothing, giving all to kin.

sentences.zh: 性儉率，居處服用充足而已，不事華侈。

translations.literal: His nature was plain and direct; dwelling and dress were sufficient only, without luxury.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly, without luxury.

sentences.zh: 晚年頗好音樂，有妓妾十數人，並無被服姿容。

translations.literal: In later years he rather loved music; he had a dozen concubines without fine dress or looks.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he loved music; a dozen plain concubines.

sentences.zh: 每有客，常隔簾奏之，時謂簾為夏侯妓衣。

translations.literal: Whenever he had guests he would play behind a curtain; at the time they called the curtain "Xiahou's entertainers' dress."
translations.idiomatic: For guests he played behind a curtain—men called it Xiahou's entertainers' dress.

sentences.zh: 子誼襲封豐城縣公。

translations.literal: At the time Qiao Inspector Zhan Sengzhi besieged East Yuzhou Inspector Yuan Qinghe at Guangling and entered the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao inspector Zhan Sengzhi besieged Yuan Qinghe at Guangling and entered the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 亶弟 夔

translations.literal: Wei general Yuan Xianbo led an army to relieve; Sengzhi met and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xianbo came to relieve; Sengzhi defeated him.

sentences.zh: 亶弟夔字季龍，位大匠卿，累遷司州刺史，領安陸太守。

translations.literal: Kui from Wuyang came to join Sengzhi and cut the Wei army's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Kui came from Wuyang, joined Sengzhi, and cut Wei retreat.

sentences.zh: 帥壯武將軍裴之禮、直閣將軍任思祖出義陽道，攻平靜、穆陵、陰山三關，克之。

translations.literal: Qinghe within built palisades to hold firm; when Kui arrived he requested surrender; in all men and women numbering over ten thousand mouths surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe held within; when Kui came he surrendered—more than ten thousand people.

sentences.zh: 時譙州刺史湛僧智圍東豫州刺史元慶和於廣陵，入其郛。

translations.literal: Xianbo heard it and fled by night; the host pursued and captured over twenty thousand, kills and captures beyond counting—thereafter the northern route of Yiyang was cut off from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbo fled by night; pursuit took twenty thousand; Yiyang's north road was severed from Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏將元顯伯率軍赴援，僧智逆擊破之。

translations.literal: When Yingzhou Inspector Yuan Yuanda surrendered, edict changed it to North Sizhou; Kui was made inspector with overall command of Sizhou, enfeoffed Marquis of Baocheng County.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanda surrendered, the region became North Sizhou; Kui was inspector and Marquis of Baocheng.

sentences.zh: 夔自武陽出會僧智，斷魏軍歸路。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhongtong he was Yuzhou Inspector with overall command added.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong year six he held Yuzhou with overall command.

sentences.zh: 慶和於內築柵自固，及夔至遂請降，凡降男女口萬餘人。

translations.literal: Yuzhou had seen war year after year and the people mostly lost their livelihoods; Kui then led soldiers to build a dam at Cangling, irrigating over a thousand qing of fields, harvesting over a million shi of grain yearly to fill stores and aid the poor—the territory relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: War had ruined Yuzhou; Kui dammed Cangling, irrigated a thousand qing, stored a million shi, and fed the poor.

sentences.zh: 顯伯聞之夜遁，眾軍追虜二萬餘人，斬獲不可勝數，由是義陽北道遂與魏絕。

translations.literal: Dan had earlier held this post; now Kui again dwelt there—brothers both had favor in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had held the post before; now Kui—both brothers were loved in the land.

sentences.zh: 及郢州刺史元願達降，詔改為北司州，以夔為刺史，兼督司州，封保城縣侯。

translations.literal: The people sang, "To have a province, again and again we get Xiahou. Elder brother, younger brother—their rule is excellent."
translations.idiomatic: The people sang, "For a province we keep getting Xiahou—brother after brother, gentle rule."

sentences.zh: 中大通六年，為豫州刺史，加督。

translations.literal: Seven years in the province; far and near many attached to him; he had a household guard of ten thousand men and two thousand horses, all trained and strong—the greatest force of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years in office he gathered ten thousand retainers and two thousand horses—the strongest host of the day.

sentences.zh: 豫州積歲連兵，人頗失業，夔乃率軍人于蒼陵立堰，溉田千餘頃，歲收谷百餘萬石，以充儲備，兼贍貧人，境內賴之。

translations.literal: His nature was luxurious; rear chambers had a hundred concubines trailing brocade and gold and kingfisher ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Luxurious, with a hundred concubines in brocade and gold.

sentences.zh: 夔兄亶先經此任，至是夔又居焉，兄弟並有恩惠於鄉里。

translations.literal: He loved worthy men and did not hold himself high for rank; civil and military guests constantly filled his seats—at the time he was praised for this too.
translations.idiomatic: He loved talent, kept a full hall of guests, and was praised for it.

sentences.zh: 百姓歌曰：「我之有州，頻得夏侯。

translations.literal: He died in the province; posthumous title Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in post; posthumous name Huan.

sentences.zh: 前兄後弟，布政優優。」

translations.literal: His son Zhuan succeeded, reaching Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuan rose to minister of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 夔在州七年，遠近多附之，有部曲萬人，馬二千匹，並服習精強，為當時之盛。

translations.literal: Kui's son Zhuan's younger brother Bo
translations.idiomatic: Kui's son Zhuan's younger brother Bo

sentences.zh: 性奢豪，後房伎妾曳羅綺飾金翠者百數。

translations.literal: Zhuan's younger brother Bo, in youth coarse and dangerously thin in conduct, often stayed in the countryside leading his father's household troops as provincial assistant defense.
translations.idiomatic: Bo, coarse in youth, led his father's troops in the countryside as assistant defense.

sentences.zh: 愛好人士，不以貴位自高，文武賓客常滿坐，時亦以此稱之。

translations.literal: Inspector the Marquis of Zhenyang Ming took him as prefectural chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Ming of Zhenyang made him chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 卒於州，諡曰桓。

translations.literal: When Ming was held prisoner by Wei, he again became Hou Jing's chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming was taken by Wei, Bo became Hou Jing's chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 子撰嗣，官至太僕卿。

translations.literal: When Jing rebelled, Bo was vanguard crossing the river, encamped at Shilin Lodge, broke mansions and wealthy houses of residents, seizing sons and daughters and goods entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing rebelled, Bo crossed first, camped at Shilin, looted mansions and families.

sentences.zh: 夔子撰弟 譒

translations.literal: Ming in the province had four concubines—Zhang, Yu, Wang, and Ruan—all of national beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Ming had four famous beauties: Zhang, Yu, Wang, and Ruan.

sentences.zh: 撰弟譒，少粗險薄行，常停鄉里，領其父部曲，為州助防。

translations.literal: When Ming was held by Wei, the concubines all returned to the capital mansion; when Bo arrived he broke the mansion and took them in.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming was captive the women were in the capital; Bo broke in and took them.

sentences.zh: 刺史貞陽侯明引為府長史。

translations.literal: Yu Hong was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hong

sentences.zh: 明被魏囚，復為侯景長史。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi tall, fair and clear with fine looks.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet, fair and handsome.

sentences.zh: 景反，譒前驅濟江，頓兵士林館，破邸第及居人富室，子女財貨盡略有之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns and was often army point.
translations.idiomatic: He often led the van in campaigns.

sentences.zh: 明在州有四妾章、于、王、阮，並有國色。

translations.literal: He successively held Nanqiao, Xuyi, and Jingling as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He held Nanqiao, Xuyi, and Jingling.

sentences.zh: 明被魏囚，其妾並還都第，譒至破第納焉。

translations.literal: He once told others, "My holding a commandery has four exhaustions: fish and turtles in the waters exhausted, roe deer and elk in the mountains exhausted, grain in the fields exhausted, and village people exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "In a commandery I exhaust everything—waters, mountains, fields, and people."

sentences.zh: 魚弘，襄陽人。

translations.literal: A man lives like light dust on weak grass, a white colt passing a crack.
translations.idiomatic: Life is dust on grass, a white colt through a crack.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，白澈美姿容。

translations.literal: Life is only joy—when is wealth and honor?"
translations.idiomatic: Only joy matters—when is wealth?"

sentences.zh: 累從征討，常為軍鋒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he indulged in feasting without restraint."
translations.idiomatic: Then he gave himself to unrestrained feasting."

sentences.zh: 曆南譙、盱眙、竟陵太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he indulged in feasting without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Then he gave himself to feasting without restraint.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人曰：「我為郡有四盡：水中魚鱉盡，山中獐鹿盡，田中米穀盡，村里人庶盡。

translations.literal: Over a hundred serving women, unable to bear all the gold and kingfisher; clothes, playthings, carriages and horses—all wonders of the age.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred concubines in gold and kingfisher, with clothes, toys, and carriages that were wonders of the age.

sentences.zh: 丈夫生如輕塵棲弱草，白駒之過隙。

translations.literal: He had a sleeping couch entirely of carved cypress, all four sides alike without difference, with feet of double silver openwork flowers, longevity and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: His bed was carved cypress throughout, every side alike, with double silver openwork feet of longevity and blessing.

sentences.zh: 人生但歡樂，富貴在何時。」

translations.literal: As Western Adjutant Marshal to the Prince of Xiangdong, on duty going west, on the road food ran short; along the way he picked water chestnuts and made chestnut-rice for his command.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiangdong's western adjutant marshal he went west on duty; food ran short and he fed his men on wild chestnuts along the road.

sentences.zh: 於是恣意酣賞。

translations.literal: Also on a desolate isle he caught several hundred monkeys, salted them as dried meat for drink and food.
translations.idiomatic: On a barren isle he took hundreds of monkeys and salted them for feast and cup.

sentences.zh: 侍妾百餘人，不勝金翠，服翫車馬，皆窮一時之驚絕。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Jiangling, supplies were restored again.
translations.idiomatic: By Jiangling his supplies had recovered.

sentences.zh: 有眠床一張，皆是蹙柏，四面周匝，無一有異，通用銀鏤金花壽福兩重為腳。
