translations.literal: Meeting edict to welcome the auspicious image, the prince ordered the image sent to the capital; Hong led several hundred household troops all in brocade robes, splendid along the road—many envied it.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to escort a sacred image to the capital, he marched hundreds of retainers in brocade, splendid enough to draw every eye.

sentences.zh: 為湘東王鎮西司馬，述職西上，道中乏食，緣路采菱，作菱米飯給所部。

translations.literal: As Western Adjutant Marshal to the Prince of Xiangdong, on duty going west, on the road food ran short; along the way he picked water chestnuts and made chestnut-rice for his command.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiangdong's western adjutant marshal he went west; food ran short and he fed his men on chestnuts gathered along the road.

sentences.zh: 弘度之所，後人覓一菱不得。

translations.literal: Where Hong passed, later men could not find a single water chestnut.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong passed, no one could find a single chestnut.

sentences.zh: 又於窮洲之上，捕得數百獼猴，膊以為脯，以供酒食。

translations.literal: Also on a desolate isle he caught several hundred monkeys, salted them as dried meat for drink and food.
translations.idiomatic: On a barren isle he took hundreds of monkeys and salted them for feast and cup.

sentences.zh: 比及江陵，資食復振。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Jiangling, supplies were restored again.
translations.idiomatic: By Jiangling his supplies had recovered.

sentences.zh: 逢敕迎瑞像，王令送像下都，弘率部曲數百，悉衣錦袍，赫弈滿道，頗為人所慕。

translations.literal: Meeting edict to welcome the auspicious image, the prince ordered the image sent to the capital; Hong led several hundred household troops all in brocade robes, splendid along the road—many envied it.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to escort a sacred image to the capital, he marched hundreds of retainers in brocade, splendid enough to draw every eye.

sentences.zh: 塗經夏首，李抗斅其為人，抗舅元法僧聞之，杖抗三百。

translations.literal: Passing Xiakou, Li Kang despised his conduct; Kang's uncle Yuan Faseng heard and beat Kang three hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiakou, Li Kang sneered at him; Kang's uncle Yuan Faseng had Kang thrashed three hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 後為新興、永甯太守，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he was Administrator of Xinxing and Yongning and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as prefect of Xinxing and Yongning and died in office.

sentences.zh: 起士瞻

translations.literal: Shi Zhan
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhan

sentences.zh: 初，士瞻為荊府城局參軍，浚萬人仗庫防池，得一金革鉤，隱起鏤甚精巧。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhan was Jing Prefecture city-bureau army commander; he dredged the ten-thousand weapons store moat for defense and obtained a gold belt hook, hidden relief carving extremely fine.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Jing's city-bureau commander, he dredged the arsenal moat and found a finely worked gold belt hook.

sentences.zh: 篆文曰：「錫爾金鉤，且公且侯。」

translations.literal: The inscription read, "Bestowed on you this gold hook—both duke and marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription ran, "Bestowed this gold hook—duke and marquis alike.

sentences.zh: 士瞻娶夏侯詳兄女，女竊以與詳，詳喜佩之。

translations.literal: Zhan married the elder brother's daughter of Xiahou Xiang; the woman secretly gave it to Xiang; Xiang delightedly wore it.
translations.idiomatic: He married Xiang's niece, who slipped the hook to Xiang, who wore it with delight.

sentences.zh: 及是革命，詳果封侯，而士瞻不錫茅土。

translations.literal: At the revolution Xiang indeed was enfeoffed marquis, while Zhan received no fief.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne changed, Xiang was enfeoffed; Zhan received no fief.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，入為直合將軍，歷位秦、梁二州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he entered as Direct Attendant General and successively held Qin and Liang as Inspector with overall command added.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year two he entered as direct attendant general, then inspector of Qin and Liang with overall command.

sentences.zh: 後為太子右衛率，又出為西陽、武昌二郡太守。

translations.literal: Later he was Crown Prince Right Guard Leader, then went out as Administrator of Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Later crown prince's right guard leader, then prefect of Xiyang and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 在郡清約，家無私積。

translations.literal: In the commanderies he was pure and sparing; the house had no private stores.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was frugal; no private hoard at home.

sentences.zh: 始士瞻夢得一積鹿皮，從而數之，有十一領。

translations.literal: At first Zhan dreamed he obtained a pile of deerskin; following it he counted—there were eleven hides.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of a pile of deerskin and counted eleven hides.

sentences.zh: 及覺喜曰：「鹿者祿也，吾當居十一祿乎。」

translations.literal: On waking he rejoiced and said, "Deer is lu (salary); I shall surely hold eleven salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Awake he said, "Deer means salary—I shall hold eleven posts.

sentences.zh: 自其仕進所蒞已九，及除二郡，心惡之，遇疾不肯療。

translations.literal: From his rise the posts he held already numbered nine; when given the two commanderies his heart hated it; he met illness and would not treat it.
translations.idiomatic: Nine posts had already come; the two commanderies displeased him; he fell ill and refused care.

sentences.zh: 普通七年卒於郡，贈左衛將軍，諡曰鬍子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Putong he died in the commandery; posthumously Left Guard General; posthumous title Huizi.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year seven he died in office; posthumously left guard general; posthumous name Huizi.

sentences.zh: 子琨時在戎役，聞問一踴而絕，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: His son Kun was then on campaign; on hearing the news he leapt once and fainted, long before reviving.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kun, on campaign, heard and fainted dead away.

sentences.zh: 不顧軍制，輒離所部，遂以孝聞。

translations.literal: Disregarding military law he left his unit; thus his filial piety became known.
translations.idiomatic: He left his post against orders and won fame for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 詔下旌異。

translations.literal: Edict went down to praise and distinguish him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 蔡道恭

translations.literal: Cai Daogong
translations.idiomatic: Cai Daogong

sentences.zh: 蔡道恭字懷儉，南陽冠軍人也。

translations.literal: Cai Daogong, styled Huaijian, was a native of Guanjun in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Daogong, courtesy name Huaijian, was from Guanjun in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 父那，宋益州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Na was Song Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Na had been Song inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，魏圍司州，時城中眾不滿五千人，食裁半歲。

translations.literal: In the third year Wei besieged Sizhou; at the time the host in the city was less than five thousand men, food barely half a year.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Wei besieged Sizhou with fewer than five thousand defenders and half a year's grain.

sentences.zh: 魏軍攻之，晝夜不息，乃作大車載土，四面俱前，欲以填塹。

translations.literal: The Wei army attacked day and night without cease; they also made great carts loaded with earth, all four sides advancing together, wishing to fill the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei attacked ceaselessly and advanced earth-filled carts to fill the moat.

sentences.zh: 道恭塹內列艨艟鬥艦以待之。

translations.literal: Daogong within the moat lined tower-ships and battle vessels to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Daogong lined tower ships in the moat to meet them.

sentences.zh: 魏人不得進，又潛作伏道以決塹水，道恭載土屯塞之。

translations.literal: The Wei men could not advance; they also secretly dug covered ways to breach the moat water; Daogong loaded earth to block it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei tried to drain the moat he blocked them with earth.

sentences.zh: 相持百餘日，前後斬獲不可勝計。

translations.literal: Stalemated over a hundred days, kills and captures before and after beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred days the slaughter was beyond count.

sentences.zh: 魏大造梯沖，攻圍日急。

translations.literal: Wei greatly built scaling ladders and assault towers; the siege grew daily urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei built siege towers; the assault grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 道恭用四石烏漆大弓射，所中皆洞甲飲羽，一發或貫兩人，敵人望弓皆靡。

translations.literal: Daogong used four-stone black-lacquer great bows to shoot; what was hit pierced armor and drank feathers; one shot sometimes transfixed two men; the enemy seeing the bow all withered.
translations.idiomatic: His four-stone black bows pierced armor; one arrow might nail two men; the enemy quailed at the bow.

sentences.zh: 又于城內作土山，多作大矟，長二丈五尺，施長刃，使壯士執以刺魏人。

translations.literal: Also within the city he made an earthen hill and many great spears two zhang five chi long with long blades, strong men wielding them to stab Wei men.
translations.idiomatic: He built an earthen mound and long spears for strong men to stab the Wei climbers.

sentences.zh: 魏軍甚憚之，將退。

translations.literal: The Wei army greatly feared it and was about to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Wei feared greatly and prepared to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 會道恭疾篤，乃呼兄子僧勰、從弟靈恩及將率謂曰：「吾所苦勢不能久，汝等當以死固節，無令吾沒有遺恨。」

translations.literal: It happened Daogong's illness grew grave; he then called his elder brother's son Sengji, younger cousin Ling'en, and commanders and said, "The illness I suffer cannot last long; you must with death hold the post and not let me die with regrets.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened he told his kin and officers to hold the city unto death.

sentences.zh: 又令取所持節授僧勰曰：「稟命出疆，既不得奉以還朝，方欲攜之同逝。

translations.literal: He also ordered them to take the staff of authority he held and give it to Sengji, saying, "Receiving mandate to go beyond the border, I could not bring it back to court; I now wish to carry it with me in death. It may follow the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Sengji his staff of authority to die with the coffin.

sentences.zh: 可與棺柩相隨。」

translations.literal: All wept."
translations.idiomatic: All wept.

sentences.zh: 眾皆流涕。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 其年五月卒。

translations.literal: Wei knew Daogong was dead and pressed the attack more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of his death, Wei pressed harder.

sentences.zh: 魏知道恭死，攻之轉急。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had sent Yingzhou Inspector Cao Jingzong to relieve; Jingzong did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzong had been sent to relieve but did not move.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷遣郢州刺史曹景宗赴援，景宗不前。

translations.literal: By the eighth month grain in the city was exhausted and Wei took it.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth month the city starved and fell.

sentences.zh: 至八月，城內糧盡，魏克之。

translations.literal: Posthumously General Who Pacifies the West, and they also sought to redeem the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously general who pacifies the west; the court sought his coffin.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮西將軍，並尋購喪櫬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Wei permitted return of Daogong's remains; his family traded female musicians for them.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Wei returned the body; the family traded musicians for it.

sentences.zh: 八年，魏許還道恭喪，其家以女樂易之。

translations.literal: Buried at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Buried at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 葬襄陽。

translations.literal: The enfeoffment passed to grandson Gu; he died young and the state was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to grandson Gu, who died young and the fief ended.

sentences.zh: 傳國至孫固，早卒，國除。

translations.literal: Yang Gongze
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze

sentences.zh: 楊公則

translations.literal: Yang Gongze
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze

sentences.zh: 楊公則字君翼，天水西縣人也。

translations.literal: Yang Gongze, styled Junyi, was a native of Xi County in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze, courtesy name Junyi, was from Xi County in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父仲懷，為宋豫州刺史殷琰將。

translations.literal: His father Zhonghuai was a general to Song Yuzhou Inspector Yin Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhonghuai was a general to Yin Yan of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 琰叛，輔國將軍劉勉討琰，仲懷力戰，死於橫塘。

translations.literal: When Yan rebelled, Supporting-the-State General Liu Mian attacked Yan; Zhonghuai fought fiercely and died at Hengtang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan rebelled, Liu Mian attacked; Zhonghuai died at Hengtang.

sentences.zh: 公則隨父在軍，年未弱冠，冒陣抱屍，號哭氣絕良久。

translations.literal: Gongze followed his father in the army; before the capping age he dashed into the ranks and embraced the corpse, wailing until breath stopped for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Still a boy, he ran into the fight, seized his father's corpse, and wailed until he fainted.

sentences.zh: 勉命還仲懷首。

translations.literal: Mian ordered return of Zhonghuai's head.
translations.idiomatic: Mian sent back the head.

sentences.zh: 公則斂畢，徒步負喪歸鄉里，由此著名。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete, he went on foot bearing the coffin home to the village—thereby he became famous.
translations.idiomatic: He bore the coffin home on foot and became famous.

sentences.zh: 後梁州刺史范柏年板為宋熙太守、領白馬戍主。

translations.literal: Later Liangzhou Inspector Fan Bonian appointed him Administrator of Songxi, also in charge of the White Horse garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bonian of Liangzhou made him prefect of Songxi and warden of White Horse.

sentences.zh: 時氐賊李烏奴攻白馬，公則矢盡糧竭，陷於寇，抗聲罵賊，烏奴壯之，耍與同事。

translations.literal: Gongze falsely agreed and plotted; the plot leaked; he fled alone on one horse.
translations.idiomatic: He pretended agreement, plotted escape, and fled alone when discovered.

sentences.zh: 公則偽許而圖之，謀泄，單馬逃歸。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi issued edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Emperor Gao praised him by edict.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝下詔褒美。

translations.literal: Made Administrator of Jinshou; in office he was pure and self-restraining.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jinshou he was scrupulously clean.

sentences.zh: 除晉壽太守，在任清潔自守。

translations.literal: Moved to Administrator of Fufeng; on mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Fufeng and left on his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 遷扶風太守，母憂去官。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Inspector Chen Xianda raised him as Pacifying-the-North General and again gave him the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda of Yongzhou restored him as pacifying-the-north general and prefect.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史陳顯達起為甯朔將軍，復領太守。

translations.literal: Shortly, Jingzhou Inspector the Prince of Badong Zixiang raised rebellion; Gongze advanced to suppress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Badong rebelled, Gongze marched against him.

sentences.zh: 頃之，荊州刺史巴東王子響構亂，公則進討。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was moved to Administrator of Wuning; the people were at ease with him.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt he was prefect of Wuning, where the people were content.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷武甯太守，百姓便之。

translations.literal: He entered as Forward Army General.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as forward army general.

sentences.zh: 入為前軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor He was Jingzhou Inspector, Gongze was Western Central Commandant Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He was inspector of Jingzhou, Gongze was his army commander.

sentences.zh: 和帝為荊州刺史，公則為西中郎中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor He was Jingzhou Inspector, Gongze was Western Central Commandant Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He was inspector of Jingzhou, Gongze was his army commander.

sentences.zh: 及蕭穎胄協同梁武，以公則為輔國將軍，領西中郎諮議參軍，率兵東下。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yingzhou joined Liang Wudi, Gongze was made Supporting-the-State General, Western Central Commandant Adviser, leading troops east.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzhou joined Wudi, Gongze was made supporting-the-state general and adviser, marching east.

sentences.zh: 和帝即位，授湘州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor He ascended, he was appointed Xiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He ascended, he was made inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁武軍次沔口，公則率湘府之眾會于夏口。

translations.literal: Liang Wudi's army halted at Hankou; Gongze led Xiang forces to assemble at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi halted at Hankou; Gongze led Xiang troops to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 時荊州諸軍悉受公則節度，雖蕭穎達宗室之貴亦隸焉。

translations.literal: At the time all Jingzhou armies were under Gongze's command—even the honored clansman Xiao Yingda was subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: All Jingzhou armies were under his command—even Yingda of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 郢城平，武帝命眾軍即日俱下，公則受命先驅。

translations.literal: When Ying city fell, Wudi ordered all armies to march down the same day; Gongze received orders as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying fell, Wudi ordered an immediate march; Gongze led the van.

sentences.zh: 江州既定，連旌東下，直造建鄴。

translations.literal: When Jiangzhou was settled, banners linked east straight to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou secured, he marched straight on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 公則號令嚴明，秋豪不犯，所在莫不賴焉。

translations.literal: Gongze's orders were strict and clear; not a hair was harmed—wherever he went all relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were strict; nothing was harmed—everywhere people relied on him.

sentences.zh: 大軍至新林，公則自越城移屯領軍府壘北樓，與南掖門相對。

translations.literal: When the great army reached Xinlin, Gongze moved from Yuecheng to encamp at the north tower of the Army Leader's fortress, opposite the South Flank Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinlin he encamped at the army leader's north tower, facing the South Flank Gate.

sentences.zh: 嘗登樓望戰，城中遙見麾蓋，縱神鋒弩射之，矢貫胡床，左右皆失色。

translations.literal: Once he ascended the tower to watch the battle; the city from afar saw his banners and canopy and loosed divine-bolt crossbows; an arrow pierced his armrest and all around paled.
translations.idiomatic: Watching battle from the tower, the enemy shot divine-bolt bolts; one pierced his armrest and his men paled.

sentences.zh: 公則曰：「虜幾中吾腳。」

translations.literal: Gongze said, "The bandits nearly hit my foot."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The enemy nearly hit my foot."

sentences.zh: 談笑如初。

translations.literal: He talked and laughed as before.
translations.idiomatic: He laughed and talked as before.

sentences.zh: 東昏夜選勇士攻公則柵，軍中驚擾。

translations.literal: Dong Hun by night selected brave men to attack Gongze's palisade; the army was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun's night attack alarmed the camp.

sentences.zh: 公則堅臥不起，徐命擊之，東昏軍乃退。

translations.literal: Gongze lay firm and did not rise, slowly ordered a strike, and Dong Hun's army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He lay still, then ordered a counterattack and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 公則所領多是湘溪人，性懦怯，城內輕之，以為易與，每出蕩，輒先犯公則壘。

translations.literal: Those Gongze led were mostly men of Xiang Creek, timid by nature; within the city they were slighted as easy targets—whenever they sallied they first struck Gongze's ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: His Xiang Creek men were thought timid; the city always hit his ramparts first.

sentences.zh: 公則獎厲軍士，克獲更多。

translations.literal: Gongze encouraged the soldiers and captured more.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged his men and took more captives.

sentences.zh: 及城平，城內出者或被剝奪，公則親率麾下，列陳東掖門，衛送公卿士庶，故出者多由公則營焉。

translations.literal: When the city fell, those who came out were sometimes stripped; Gongze personally led his command, arrayed at the East Flank Gate, escorted nobles and commoners—thus most who left passed through Gongze's camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he guarded the East Flank Gate and escorted nobles and commoners through his lines.

sentences.zh: 進號左將軍，還鎮南藩。

translations.literal: Advanced in rank to Left General; returned to guard the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to left general; returned to guard the south.

sentences.zh: 初，公則東下，湘部諸郡多未賓從，及公則還州，然後諸屯聚並散。

translations.literal: Earlier when Gongze marched east, many Xiang commanderies had not yet submitted; when Gongze returned to the province, then all garrison clusters dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Many Xiang districts had held out; when he returned they submitted.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，進號平南將軍，封甯都縣侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was advanced to Pacifying-the-South General, enfeoffed Marquis of Ningdu County.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year one he was pacifying-the-south general, Marquis of Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 湘州寇亂累年，人多流散。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou had seen raids and chaos for years; many people scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou had been ravaged for years; people had scattered.

sentences.zh: 公則輕刑薄斂，頃之戶口充復。

translations.literal: Gongze lightened punishments and taxes; soon households were restored.
translations.idiomatic: He lightened punishments and taxes; households soon returned.

sentences.zh: 為政雖無威嚴，然勵己廉慎，為吏人所悅。

translations.literal: In government though without fierce severity, he disciplined himself in integrity and caution—clerks and people were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Without harsh rule he was scrupulously honest—clerks and people were pleased.

sentences.zh: 湘俗單門多以賂求州職，公則至皆斷之，所辟皆州郡著姓。

translations.literal: Xiang custom: humble houses often bribed for provincial posts; when Gongze arrived he cut all off and appointed only prominent provincial kin.
translations.idiomatic: He ended bribery for office and appointed only reputable local families.

sentences.zh: 武帝班下諸州以為法。

translations.literal: Wudi issued it to all provinces as law.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi made it the model for all provinces.

sentences.zh: 三年，征中護軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned as Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was summoned as central army commander.

sentences.zh: 代至，乘二舸便發，送故一無所取。

translations.literal: When his replacement arrived, he took two light boats and set out; farewell gifts he took none.
translations.idiomatic: When relieved he sailed off in two light boats, taking no farewell gifts.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Moved to Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He became commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷始議北侵，公則威名素著，至都，詔假節，先屯洛口。

translations.literal: When the court first debated northern invasion, Gongze's martial name was long renowned; on reaching the capital, edict lent him staff of authority to encamp first at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: When the north was debated, his fame brought him to the capital with authority to hold Luokou.

sentences.zh: 公則受命將發，遘疾，謂親人曰：「昔廉頗、馬援以年老見遺，猶自力請用。

translations.literal: Gongze received orders to set out but met illness; he told kin, "Once Lian Po and Ma Yuan were set aside for age yet strove to be used.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to march but ill, he told kin, "Lian Po and Ma Yuan were cast aside in age yet still wished to serve.

sentences.zh: 今國家不以吾朽懦，任以前驅，方于古人，見知重矣。

translations.literal: Now the state does not treat me as decayed and weak but charges me as vanguard—compared to the ancients, the trust is heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The state still trusts me as vanguard—that is heavy honor.

sentences.zh: 雖臨塗疾苦，豈可僶俛辭事。

translations.literal: Though on the road I am afflicted, how can I bow out of the task.
translations.idiomatic: Though ill on the road, how can I refuse.

sentences.zh: 馬革還葬，此吾志也。」

translations.literal: Burial in horse-hide—this is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Burial in horse-hide is my wish."

sentences.zh: 遂強起登舟，至洛口，壽春士女歸降者數千戶。

translations.literal: He forced himself to board ship; reaching Luokou, Shouchun men and women numbering several thousand households surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He forced himself aboard; at Luokou thousands of Shouchun households surrendered.

sentences.zh: 魏豫州刺史薛恭度遣長史石榮等前鋒接戰，即斬石榮，逐北至壽春，去城數十里而返。

translations.literal: Wei Yuzhou Inspector Xue Gongdu sent Chief of Staff Shi Rong and others as vanguard to meet in battle; he at once beheaded Shi Rong, pursued north to Shouchun, several tens of li from the city and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Shi Rong, pursued to Shouchun, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，卒于師。

translations.literal: Illness grave, he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the army of his illness.

sentences.zh: 武帝深痛惜之，即日舉哀，諡烈侯。

translations.literal: Wudi deeply mourned him, that same day raised mourning, posthumous title Fierce Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi mourned him the same day; posthumous name Fierce Marquis.

sentences.zh: 公則為人敦厚慈愛，居家篤睦，視兄子過於己子，家財悉委焉。

translations.literal: Gongze was generous and loving in person, harmonious at home, treated elder brother's sons better than his own sons, and entrusted all family wealth to them.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous at home and favored his brother's sons over his own, giving them all his wealth.

sentences.zh: 性好學，雖居軍旅，手不輟卷，士大夫以此稱之。

translations.literal: He loved learning; though in the army he never laid aside books—scholar-officials praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books even in camp—scholars praised him.

sentences.zh: 子瞟嗣，有罪國除。

translations.literal: His son Piao succeeded; for crime the state was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Piao inherited; for crime the fief ended.

sentences.zh: 帝以公則勳臣，特聽庶長子眺嗣。

translations.literal: The Emperor, as Gongze was a merit minister, specially permitted the eldest son of a concubine, Tiao, to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi allowed his concubine's eldest son Tiao to succeed.

sentences.zh: 眺固讓歷年，乃受。

translations.literal: Tiao firmly declined for years, then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao declined for years, then accepted.

sentences.zh: 鄧元起

translations.literal: Deng Yuanqi
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuanqi

sentences.zh: 初，梁武之起，益州刺史劉季連持兩端。

translations.literal: Earlier when Liang Wudi rose, Yizhou Inspector Liu Jilian held both ends.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi rose, Liu Jilian of Yizhou wavered.

sentences.zh: 及聞元起至，遂發兵拒守。

translations.literal: On hearing Yuanqi had arrived, he then sent troops to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Yuanqi had come, he sent troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 元起至巴西，巴西太守朱士略開門以待。

translations.literal: Yuanqi reached Baxi; Baxi Administrator Zhu Shilue opened the gates to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: At Baxi, Administrator Zhu Shilue opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 先時蜀人多逃亡，至是競出投元起，皆稱起義應朝廷。

translations.literal: Earlier many Shu people had fled; now they all rushed out to join Yuanqi, all calling it rising for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Shu fugitives now flocked to him as loyalists to the court.

sentences.zh: 元起在道久，軍糧乏絕，或說之曰：「蜀郡政慢，若檢巴西一郡籍注，因而罰之，所獲必厚。」

translations.literal: Yuanqi had been on the road long; army grain was exhausted; some said to him, "Shu government is lax—if you audit Baxi commandery registers and punish accordingly, the gain will be great."
translations.idiomatic: Grain ran out; some urged auditing Baxi registers for heavy fines.

sentences.zh: 元起然之。

translations.literal: Yuanqi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi agreed.

sentences.zh: 涪令李膺諫曰：「使君前有嚴敵，後無繼援，山人始附，於我觀德。

translations.literal: Fou Magistrate Li Ying admonished, "Your lordship has fierce enemies before and no relief behind; mountain folk have just attached—they watch your virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Li Ying warned, "Enemies ahead, no relief behind—the mountain folk watch your virtue.

sentences.zh: 若糾以刻薄，人必不堪。

translations.literal: If you are too harsh, the people cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: If you are too harsh, the people cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 眾心一離，雖悔無及。

translations.literal: When hearts depart, though you regret it, it is too late.
translations.idiomatic: When hearts depart, regret comes too late.

sentences.zh: 膺請出圖之，不患資糧不足也。」

translations.literal: Ying requested to go map it; he was not afraid of scarce provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Ying asked to survey the land and did not fear short supplies.

sentences.zh: 元起曰：「善，一以委卿。」

translations.literal: Yuanqi said, "Good—I entrust it entirely to you."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi said, "Good—I entrust it all to you."

sentences.zh: 膺退，率富人上軍資米，俄得三萬斛。

translations.literal: Ying withdrew and led the wealthy to submit army grain; soon thirty thousand shi were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Ying led the wealthy to submit grain; soon thirty thousand shi were gathered.

sentences.zh: 元起進屯西平，季連始嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Yuanqi advanced to encamp at Xiping; Jilian at last walled himself in for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi encamped at Xiping; Jilian finally walled himself in.

sentences.zh: 時益州兵亂既久，人廢耕農，內外苦饑，人多相食，道路斷絕。

translations.literal: At the time Yi rebels had long raged; people had abandoned farming; within and without they suffered famine; many ate one another; roads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: War had ruined farming; famine was so fierce men ate one another; roads were cut.

sentences.zh: 季連計窮。

translations.literal: Jilian was at his wits' end.
translations.idiomatic: Jilian was desperate.

sentences.zh: 會明年武帝使赦季連罪，許之降，季連即日開城納元起，元起送季連于建康。

translations.literal: It happened the next year the Emperor sent edict pardoning Jilian's crime and permitted surrender; Jilian that day opened the city to receive Yuanqi; Yuanqi sent Jilian to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Next year an edict pardoned Jilian; he opened the city; Yuanqi sent him to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 元起以鄉人庾黔婁為錄事參軍，又得荊州刺史蕭遙欣故客蔣光濟，並厚待之，任以州事。

translations.literal: Yuanqi made fellow townsman Yu Qianlou Recorder and also obtained former Jingzhou client Jiang Guangji—both were generously treated and entrusted with provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made Yu Qianlou recorder and Jiang Guangji his adviser—both were trusted for provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 黔婁甚清潔，光濟多計謀，並勸為善政。

translations.literal: Qianlou was very pure; Guangji was full of schemes—both urged good government.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlou was pure; Guangji was clever—both urged good government.

sentences.zh: 元起之克季連也，城內財寶無所私，勸恤人事，口不論財色。

translations.literal: When Yuanqi overcame Jilian, he took no private treasure from the city; he encouraged and comforted people; he did not speak of wealth or women.
translations.idiomatic: He took no loot; he comforted the people and never spoke of wealth or women.

sentences.zh: 性能飲酒，至一斛不亂，及是絕之，為蜀土所稱。

translations.literal: By nature he could drink a hu without disorder; from then he stopped drinking—Shu for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He could drink a hu without stumbling; then he stopped—Shu praised him.

sentences.zh: 元起舅子梁矜孫性輕脫，與庾黔婁志行不同，乃言於元起曰：「城中稱有三刺史，節下何以堪之。」

translations.literal: Yuanqi's nephew Liang Jinsun was frivolous; unlike Qianlou in conduct; he said to Yuanqi, "In the city they say there are three inspectors—how can you, my lord, bear it?
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Jinsun was frivolous and said three men ruled the province—how could Yuanqi bear it?

sentences.zh: 元起由此疏黔婁而政跡稍損。

translations.literal: From this Yuanqi distanced Qianlou and his governance slightly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi distanced Qianlou and his rule slipped.

sentences.zh: 在政二年，以母老乞歸供養，詔許焉。

translations.literal: Two years in office he begged return to support his mother; edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he asked to go home for his mother; edict allowed it.

sentences.zh: 徵為右衛將軍，以西昌侯蕭藻代之。

translations.literal: Summoned as Right Guard General; Marquis of Xichang Xiao Zao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as right guard general; Xiao Zao replaced him.

sentences.zh: 時梁州長史夏侯道遷以南鄭叛，引魏將王景胤、孔陵，攻東、西晉壽，並遣告急。

translations.literal: At the time Liang Chief of Staff Xiahou Daoyian rebelled at Nanzheng, drawing Wei generals Wang Jingyin and Kong Ling to attack East and West Jinsou, both sending urgent reports.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyian rebelled at Nanzheng; Wei columns attacked Jinsou and sent urgent reports.

sentences.zh: 眾勸元起急救之。

translations.literal: Many urged Yuanqi to rescue immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Many urged immediate rescue.

sentences.zh: 元起曰：「朝廷萬里，軍不卒至，若寇賊浸淫，方須撲討，董督之任，非我而誰？

translations.literal: Yuanqi said, "The court is ten thousand li away—the army cannot arrive at once. If bandits spread, then we must strike down; the duty to supervise is mine—why hurry and press?
translations.idiomatic: He said the court was far away and he alone must supervise—why the hurry?

sentences.zh: 何事匆匆便相催督。」

translations.literal: Qianlou and others urgently admonished; he would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlou urged him; he refused.

sentences.zh: 黔婁等苦諫之，皆不從。

translations.literal: Wudi also lent Yuanqi staff of authority to command expeditionary armies to save Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi gave him authority to save Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 武帝亦假元起節、都督征討諸軍，將救漢中。

translations.literal: By then Wei had already taken both Jinsou.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wei had taken both Jinsou.

sentences.zh: 比是，魏已攻克兩晉壽。

translations.literal: When Xiao Zao was about to arrive, Yuanqi busily prepared return baggage; grain stores and equipment were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiao Zao came, Yuanqi packed to leave, stripping stores bare.

sentences.zh: 蕭藻將至，元起頗營還裝，糧儲器械略無遺者。

translations.literal: Xiao Zao entered the city and demanded his fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zao demanded his fine horses.

sentences.zh: 蕭藻入城，求其良馬。

translations.literal: Yuanqi said, "Young master—what need have you of horses?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi said, "Young man—what need of horses?"

sentences.zh: 元起曰：「年少郎子，何用馬為。」

translations.literal: Zao was furious, drunk, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zao, furious and drunk, killed him.

sentences.zh: 藻恚，醉而殺之。

translations.literal: Yuanqi's subordinates surrounded the city, weeping and asking the reason.
translations.idiomatic: His men surrounded the city weeping.

sentences.zh: 元起麾下圍城，哭且問其故。

translations.literal: Zao feared and said, "The Son of Heaven had edict."
translations.idiomatic: Zao feared and said, "The emperor ordered it."

sentences.zh: 藻懼曰：「天子有詔。」

translations.literal: The host then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The host dispersed.

sentences.zh: 眾乃散。

translations.literal: They then slandered him as rebellious; the Emperor was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: They slandered him as a rebel; the emperor doubted.

sentences.zh: 遂誣以反，帝疑焉。

translations.literal: The authorities pursued impeachment and stripped fief and land; edict halved the enfeoffment, enfeoffed Marquis of Songzi County.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities impeached him; his fief was halved to Songzi.

sentences.zh: 有司追劾削爵土，詔減邑之半，封松滋縣侯。

translations.literal: Former subordinate Luo Yan of Guanghan went to court to sue; the Emperor said, "It is indeed as I measured."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yan sued at court; the emperor said, "As I thought."

sentences.zh: 故吏廣漢羅研詣闕訟之，帝曰：「果如我所量也。」

translations.literal: He sent to reproach Zao, "Yuanqi avenged you—how is avenging the avenger filial piety?"
translations.idiomatic: He reproached Zao: "Yuanqi avenged you—how is this filial?"

sentences.zh: 使讓藻曰：「元起為汝報讎，汝為讎報讎，忠孝之道如何？

translations.literal: He then demoted Zao to General of the Champions.
translations.idiomatic: He demoted Zao to general of the champions.

sentences.zh: 「乃貶藻號為冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously Yuanqi General Who Pacifies the West, gave musical escort, posthumous title Loyal Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was general who pacifies the west; posthumous name Loyal Marquis.

sentences.zh: 贈元起征西將軍，給鼓吹，諡忠侯。

translations.literal: Luo Yan styled Shenwei; in youth he had talent and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yan, styled Shenwei, was talented and eloquent in youth.

sentences.zh: 羅研字深微，少有材辯。

translations.literal: When Yuanqi pacified Shu he recruited him as chief clerk, later Magistrate of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi made him chief clerk, later magistrate of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 元起平蜀，辟為主簿，後為信安令。

translations.literal: The old practice set Agricultural Viewing Envoys to survey mulberry and fields, troubling the people.
translations.idiomatic: Old practice sent envoys to survey fields, troubling people.

sentences.zh: 故事置觀農謁者，圍桑度田，勞擾百姓。

translations.literal: Yan requested abolishing the abuse; the Emperor followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked to end the abuse; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 研請除其弊，帝從之。

translations.literal: Loyal and Fierce Prince Hui of Poyang was coming to Shu and heard his name, asked him as Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui of Poyang heard of him and made him vice director.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽忠烈王恢臨蜀，聞其名，請為別駕。

translations.literal: When Marquis of Xichang Zao again was inspector, the province feared; Yan's bearing was calm.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao returned as inspector the province feared; Yan was calm.

sentences.zh: 及西昌侯藻重為刺史，州人為之懼，研舉止自若。

translations.literal: The marquis said to him, "Without me there is no place for you; without you there is no serving me."
translations.idiomatic: The marquis said, "Without me you have no place; without you I cannot govern."

sentences.zh: 侯謂曰：「非我無以容卿，非卿無以事我。」

translations.literal: At the Qi Gou'er affair, Marquis of Linru Hou mocked him, "You Shu people love chaos and greed—thus to this."
translations.idiomatic: Hou mocked him: "You Shu love chaos—that is why."

sentences.zh: 齊苟兒之役，臨汝侯嘲之曰：「卿蜀人樂禍貪亂，一至於此。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Shu has long accumulated abuses—not one morning's fault.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Shu's abuses are old—not one morning's fault."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「蜀中積弊，實非一朝。

translations.literal: Villages of a hundred households have fewer than a handful with food; the desperate are eight or nine in ten; bound laborers two or three in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Few villages had food; most were desperate; many were bound laborers.

sentences.zh: 百家為村，不過數家有食，窮迫之人，什有八九，束縛之使，旬有二三。

translations.literal: In villages of a hundred households fewer than a handful had food; of the destitute eight or nine in ten; of bound laborers two or three in ten.
translations.idiomatic: In a hundred-household village only a few families ate; most were destitute; many were bound to service.

sentences.zh: 貪亂樂禍，無足多怪。

translations.literal: Greed, disorder, and delight in calamity are hardly strange.
translations.idiomatic: Greed for chaos is no surprise.

sentences.zh: 若令家畜五母之雞，一母之豕，床上有百錢布被，甑中有數升麥飯，雖蘇、張巧說于前，韓、白按劍於後，將不能使一夫為盜，況貪亂乎？」

translations.literal: If each household kept five laying hens and one sow, had a hundred-cash cloth on the bed and a few sheng of wheat in the pot, though Su Qin and Zhang Yi cajoled in front and Han Xin and Bai Qi gripped swords behind, one could not make a single man a bandit—how much less wholesale disorder?"
translations.idiomatic: Give peasants hens, a sow, cloth, and grain, and even Su and Zhang could not turn them into bandits—much less a general uprising."

sentences.zh: 大通二年，為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he was Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year two he became a regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 嗣王范將西，忠烈王恢謂曰：「吾昔在蜀，每事委羅研，汝遵而勿失。」

translations.literal: Heir Prince Fan was going west; Loyal Prince Hui said, "In Shu I always entrusted matters to Luo Yan—you obey and do not fail."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fan was heading west; Prince Hui told him, "In Shu I always relied on Luo Yan—follow his counsel."

sentences.zh: 範至，復以為別駕，升堂拜母，蜀人榮之。

translations.literal: When Fan arrived, Yan was again made Vice Director; he ascended the hall to bow to Fan's mother, and the people of Shu took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan arrived, Yan was again made vice director; he bowed to Fan's mother in the hall, to Shu people's honor.

sentences.zh: 數年卒官。

translations.literal: After several years he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office after a few years.

sentences.zh: 蜀土以文達者，唯研與同郡李膺。

translations.literal: Among Shu men famed for letters, only Yan and his fellow townsman Li Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu, only Yan and Li Ying of his district were famed for learning.

sentences.zh: 膺字公胤，有才辯。

translations.literal: Ying, styled Gongyin, had talent in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying, courtesy name Gongyin, was gifted in debate.

sentences.zh: 西昌侯藻為益州，以為主簿。

translations.literal: When Marquis of Xichang Zao was in Yizhou, he made Ying chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zao of Xichang made him chief clerk in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 使至都，武帝悅之，謂曰：「今李膺何如昔李膺？」

translations.literal: Sent to the capital, Wudi was pleased and said, "How does today's Li Ying compare to the Li Ying of old?"
translations.idiomatic: At court Wudi asked how he compared to the famous Li Ying of Han."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今勝昔。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Today's is superior."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Today's is better."

sentences.zh: 問其故，對曰：「昔事桓、靈之主，今逢堯、舜之君。」

translations.literal: Asked the reason, he answered, "In the past one served the lords Huan and Ling; now one meets lords Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Because the old Li Ying served bad emperors; I serve Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其對，以如意擊席者久之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised the reply and struck the seat with his ruyi for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi praised him and struck his seat with a ruyi.

sentences.zh: 乃以為益州別駕。

translations.literal: He was then made Yizhou Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 著益州記三卷行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote Records of Yizhou in three juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote three juan of Records of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，元起在荊州，刺史隨王板元起為從事別駕，庾蓽堅執不可，元起恨之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuanqi was in Jingzhou, the inspector the Prince of Sui appointed Yuanqi Assistant and Vice Director, but Yu Bi firmly opposed it and would not agree; Yuanqi resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanqi was in Jingzhou, the Prince of Sui made him vice director, but Yu Bi blocked the appointment and Yuanqi bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及大軍至都，蓽在城內甚懼。

translations.literal: When the great army reached the capital, Bi was very frightened inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the capital, Bi was terrified inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 城平，而元起先遣迎蓽，語人曰：「庾別駕若為亂兵所殺，我無以自明。」

translations.literal: When the city was pacified, Yuanqi first sent men to welcome Bi and said to people, "If Vice Director Yu were killed by disorderly troops, I could not clear myself."
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, Yuanqi sent men to fetch Bi and said, "If Yu were killed in the fighting, I could never prove my innocence."

sentences.zh: 因厚遺之。

translations.literal: He therefore sent him rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 少時又嘗至其西沮田舍，有沙門造之乞，元起有稻幾二千斛，悉以施之，時人稱其二者有大度。

translations.literal: In his youth he also once went to his farmstead at Xiju in the west; a monk came begging; Yuanqi had nearly two thousand hu of rice and gave it all away; people of the time praised both men for great magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he visited his farm at Xiju; a monk begged food and he gave away nearly two thousand hu of rice; contemporaries praised both for their largeness of spirit.

sentences.zh: 元起初為益州，過江陵迎其母，母事道方居館，不肯出。

translations.literal: When Yuanqi first went to Yizhou, he passed Jiangling to welcome his mother; his mother practiced the Way and lived in a lodge and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: On his first posting to Yizhou he went to Jiangling for his mother; she was a Daoist living in a lodge and refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 元起拜請同行，母曰：「汝貧賤家兒忽得富貴，詎可久保。

translations.literal: Yuanqi bowed and begged her to travel together; his mother said, "You, a child of a poor and lowly family, have suddenly gained wealth and rank—how can that be kept long?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi begged her to come; she said, "You were born poor—how long can sudden riches last?

sentences.zh: 我寧死此，不能與汝共入禍敗。」

translations.literal: I would rather die here than enter ruin with you."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die here than share your downfall."

sentences.zh: 及至巴東，聞蜀亂，使蔣光濟筮之遇蹇，喟然歎曰：「吾豈鄧艾而及此乎。」

translations.literal: When they reached Badong, he heard of turmoil in Shu and had Jiang Guangji divine; he obtained Hexagram Jian and sighed, "Am I Deng Ai that I should come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: At Badong he heard Shu was in revolt and had Jiang Guangji cast the hexagram Jian; he sighed, "Am I another Deng Ai?"

sentences.zh: 後果如筮。

translations.literal: Later it turned out as the divination said.
translations.idiomatic: Events later matched the omen.

sentences.zh: 子鏗嗣。

translations.literal: His son Keng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Keng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 張惠紹

translations.literal: Zhang Huishao
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huishao

sentences.zh: 張惠紹字德繼，義陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Huishao, styled Deji, was a man of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huishao, courtesy name Deji, was from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 少有武幹，仕齊為竟陵橫桑戍主。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial talent and served Qi as garrison commander of Hengsang at Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he showed martial talent and served Qi as commander of the Hengsang garrison at Jingling.

sentences.zh: 母喪歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 聞梁武帝起兵，乃自歸，累有戰功。

translations.literal: Hearing that Liang Wudi was raising arms, he came of himself to submit and repeatedly won battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi rose in arms he joined him and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，封石陽縣侯，位驍騎將軍、直合、左細仗主。

translations.literal: When Wudi ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Shiyang County and held the posts of General of Valiant Cavalry, Direct Attendant, and Chief of the Left Fine Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At Wudi's accession he was made Marquis of Shiyang, general of valiant cavalry, direct attendant, and chief of the left fine guards.

sentences.zh: 時東昏餘黨數百人竊入南、北掖門，夜燒神獸門，害衛尉張弘策。

translations.literal: At the time several hundred remnant followers of Dong Hun secretly entered the south and north side gates, burned the Divine Beast Gate at night, and killed Commandant of the Guard Zhang Hongce.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred of Dong Hun's remnant men broke into the palace gates, burned the Divine Beast Gate, and killed Commandant Zhang Hongce.

sentences.zh: 惠紹馳率所領赴戰，賊乃散走。

translations.literal: Huishao galloped leading his command to battle and the rebels scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Huishao charged with his troops and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 遷太子右衛率，以軍功累增爵邑。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Guard of the Heir Apparent and through military merit his fief and estate were repeatedly increased.
translations.idiomatic: He became right guard of the heir apparent and his fief grew with his victories.

sentences.zh: 歷位衛尉卿，左衛將軍，司州刺史，領安陸太守。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Commandant of the Guard, Left Guard General, Inspector of Sizhou, and concurrent Administrator of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commandant of the guard, left guard general, inspector of Sizhou, and administrator of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 在州和理，吏人親愛之。

translations.literal: In the province he was harmonious and orderly; officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed harmoniously and was beloved by officials and people.

sentences.zh: 征還為左衛將軍，加通直散騎常侍，甲仗百人，直衛殿中。

translations.literal: Recalled, he became Left Guard General with added title Regular Attendant of the Palace, a hundred suits of armor, and palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as left guard general with added palace attendant rank, he commanded a hundred guards in the hall.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子澄嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 累有戰功，與湛僧智、胡紹世、魚弘並為當時驍將。

translations.literal: He repeatedly won battle merit and with Zhan Sengzhi, Hu Shaoshi, and Yu Hong was among the fierce generals of the time.
translations.idiomatic: A proven fighter, he ranked with Zhan Sengzhi, Hu Shaoshi, and Yu Hong among the day's fiercest generals.

sentences.zh: 曆官衛尉卿，太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He successively served as Commandant of the Guard and Left Guard of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of commandant of the guard and left guard of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰湣。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous name Mourned.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; posthumous name Mourned.

sentences.zh: 馮道根

translations.literal: Feng Daogen
translations.idiomatic: Feng Daogen

sentences.zh: 馮道根字巨基，廣平酇人也。

translations.literal: Feng Daogen, styled Juji, was a man of Zan in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Daogen, courtesy name Juji, was from Zan in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 少孤，家貧，傭賃以養母。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his family was poor; he hired himself out to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he hired out as a laborer to feed his mother.

sentences.zh: 行得甘肥，未嘗先食，必遽還以遺母。

translations.literal: When he obtained sweet or rich food he never ate first but hurried back to give it to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Any good food he got he brought straight home to his mother without tasting it first.

sentences.zh: 年十三，以孝聞。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen his filial piety was known through the commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡召為主簿，不就，曰：「吾當使封侯廟食，安能為儒吏邪。」

translations.literal: The commandery summoned him as chief clerk but he would not accept, saying, "I mean to win a fief and temple sacrifices—how could I be a bookish clerk?"
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as chief clerk he refused: "I will win a fief and sacrifices—why be a clerk?"

sentences.zh: 年十六，鄉人蔡道班為湖陽戍主，攻蠻錫城，反為蠻困。

translations.literal: At sixteen a townsman, Cai Daoban, was garrison commander of Huyang; he attacked the barbarian city of Xi but was in turn trapped by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he rescued Cai Daoban, garrison chief at Huyang, who had been besieged at Xi by the Man.

sentences.zh: 道根救之、匹馬轉戰，提雙劍左右奮擊，殺傷甚多，道班以免，由是知名。

translations.literal: Daogen rescued him; on a single horse he wheeled and fought, wielding twin swords and striking left and right with great fury, killing and wounding many; Daoban escaped harm and from this Daogen became known.
translations.idiomatic: Daogen rode in alone with twin swords, killed many, and freed Daoban—his fame began there.

sentences.zh: 齊建武末，魏孝文攻陷南陽等五郡。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu in Qi, Emperor Xiaowen of Wei captured Nanyang and four other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qi's Jianwu era Wei's Emperor Xiaowen took Nanyang and four other commanderies.

sentences.zh: 明帝遣太尉陳顯達爭之，師入汮口，道根說顯達曰：「汮水急，不如悉棄船於酇城，方道步進。」

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Grand Commandant Chen Xianda to contest them; the army entered the mouth of the Bian; Daogen advised Xianda, saying, "The Bian current is swift—better to abandon all boats at Zan city and advance by land."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Chen Xianda; at the Bian mouth Daogen urged abandoning the fleet and marching overland from Zan."

sentences.zh: 顯達不聽，道根猶以私屬從軍。

translations.literal: Xianda would not listen; Daogen still followed the army as a private retainer.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda refused; Daogen followed anyway as a volunteer.

sentences.zh: 及顯達敗夜走，賴道根指路以全。

translations.literal: When Xianda was defeated and fled by night, they relied on Daogen pointing the way to escape whole.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianda fled by night, Daogen's guidance saved the column.

sentences.zh: 尋為汮口戍副。

translations.literal: Soon he was deputy garrison commander at the Bian mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He became deputy commander at the Bian mouth garrison.

sentences.zh: 以母喪還家。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 聞梁武帝起兵，乃謂所親曰：「金革奪禮，古人不避，揚名後世，豈非孝乎。」

translations.literal: Hearing that Liang Wudi was raising arms, he said to those close to him, "War suspends mourning rites—ancients did not shun it; to win fame in later ages—is that not filial?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wudi rose he told kin, "The ancients fought through mourning—fame is also filial piety."

sentences.zh: 因率鄉人歸武帝，隸于王茂，常為前鋒。

translations.literal: He therefore led his townspeople to join Wudi, attached to Wang Mao, and was often in the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He led his neighbors to Wudi, served under Wang Mao, and usually fought in the van.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，為驍騎將軍，封增城縣男。

translations.literal: When Wudi took the throne, he was made General of Valiant Cavalry and enfeoffed Baron of Zengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: At Wudi's accession he became general of valiant cavalry and baron of Zengcheng.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，為南梁太守，領阜陵城戍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was Administrator of Nanliang and concurrently held the garrison of Fuling city.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year two he governed Nanliang and held the Fuling garrison.

sentences.zh: 初到阜陵，修城隍，遠斥候，如敵將至者。

translations.literal: When he first reached Fuling he repaired walls and moats and posted distant scouts as if an enemy were about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Fuling he fortified walls and posted scouts as if battle were imminent.

sentences.zh: 眾頗笑之。

translations.literal: The troops mostly laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: His men laughed at the fuss.

sentences.zh: 道根曰：「怯防勇戰，此之謂也。」

translations.literal: Daogen said, "Timid defense and brave fighting—that is the saying."
translations.idiomatic: Daogen said, "Caution in defense makes courage in battle."

sentences.zh: 修城未畢，魏將党法宗、傅豎眼率眾二萬，奄至城下，道根塹壘未固，城中眾少，莫不失色。

translations.literal: Before the walls were finished, Wei generals Dang Fazong and Fu Shuyan led twenty thousand men and suddenly reached below the city; Daogen's trenches and ramparts were not yet firm and the host in the city was few; all lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Before the works were done, twenty thousand Wei troops under Dang Fazong and Fu Shuyan appeared; the garrison panicked.

sentences.zh: 道根命開城門，緩服登城，選精銳二百人出與魏軍戰，敗之，魏軍因退。

translations.literal: Daogen ordered the city gates opened, put on plain dress and mounted the wall, chose two hundred elite men to sally against the Wei army, defeated them, and the Wei army therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the gates in plain dress, led two hundred picked men out, routed the Wei column, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 六年，魏攻鍾離，武帝詔豫州刺史韋叡救之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Wei attacked Zhongli; Wudi ordered Inspector of Yuzhou Wei Rui to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: In year six Wei besieged Zhongli; Wudi sent Wei Rui from Yuzhou to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 道根為叡前驅，至徐州，建計據邵陽洲，築壘掘塹逼魏城。

translations.literal: Daogen was Rui's vanguard; reaching Xuzhou, he devised a plan to hold Shaoyang islet, build ramparts, and dig trenches pressing the Wei city.
translations.idiomatic: As Rui's vanguard he seized Shaoyang islet and trenchworks that hemmed the Wei camp.

sentences.zh: 道根能走馬步地，計馬足以賦功，城隍立辦。

translations.literal: Daogen could pace ground at a gallop and calculate horse paces to assign work; walls and moats were set up at once.
translations.idiomatic: He paced works at a gallop and finished walls and moats in no time.

sentences.zh: 及淮水長，道根乘戰艦斷魏連橋，魏軍敗績。

translations.literal: When the Huai rose, Daogen took war junks and severed Wei's pontoon bridges; the Wei army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai flooded he cut Wei's bridges with warships and the enemy was crushed.

sentences.zh: 進爵為伯，改封豫寧縣。

translations.literal: He advanced in rank to marquis and was re-enfeoffed in Yuning County.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis of Yuning.

sentences.zh: 八年，拜豫州刺史，領汝陰太守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou and concurrently Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he became inspector of Yuzhou and administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，境內安之。

translations.literal: His government was pure and simple; within the borders all was secure.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled simply and the region was calm.

sentences.zh: 累遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly moved to Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right guard general.

sentences.zh: 道根性謹厚，木訥少言，為將能檢禦部曲。

translations.literal: Daogen by nature was cautious and thick, wooden and slow of speech; as a general he could restrain his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cautious and taciturn, he kept tight discipline over his men.

sentences.zh: 所過村陌，將士不敢虜掠。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed through villages and lanes his officers and soldiers dared not plunder.
translations.idiomatic: His troops never looted the countryside.

sentences.zh: 每征伐終不言功，其部曲或怨非之。

translations.literal: After each campaign he never spoke of merit; some in his command grumbled against it.
translations.idiomatic: He never claimed credit after battles; some of his men resented it.

sentences.zh: 道根喻曰：「明主自鑒功之多少，吾將何事。」

translations.literal: Daogen instructed them, saying, "The enlightened lord himself gauges how much merit there is—what business have I?
translations.idiomatic: He told them, "The emperor knows our merit—why should I boast?

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗指道根示尚書令沈約，美其口不論勳。

translations.literal: Wudi once pointed to Daogen to show Minister of Works Shen Yue and praised that his mouth did not discuss merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi pointed him out to Shen Yue, praising a general who never talked of his deeds.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「此陛下之大樹將軍也。」

translations.literal: Yue said, "This is Your Majesty's great-tree general.
translations.idiomatic: Yue called him "Your Majesty's great-tree general.

sentences.zh: 曆處州郡，和理清靜，為下所懷。

translations.literal: Wherever he held prefectures and commanderies he was harmonious, pure, and quiet; subordinates cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he was gentle and quiet, and subordinates loved him.

sentences.zh: 在朝廷雖貴顯，而性儉約，所居宅不修牆屋，無器服侍衛，入室則蕭然如素士之貧賤者。

translations.literal: At court though noble and exalted, by nature he was frugal; the house he lived in did not repair its walls; he had no attendants or guards; entering the rooms it was bleak as a poor scholar's.
translations.idiomatic: Though exalted at court he lived like a poor scholar—no guards, bare rooms.

sentences.zh: 當世服其清退，武帝亦雅重之。

translations.literal: The age admired his purity and withdrawal; Wudi also greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: His austerity won the age's respect and Wudi's esteem.

sentences.zh: 微時不學，既貴粗讀書，自謂少文，常慕周勃之器量。

translations.literal: In humble times he did not study; once honored he read books in rough fashion and called himself short in letters, often admiring Zhou Bo's breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Unschooled in youth, he read a little after promotion and admired Zhou Bo's magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 十六年，復為豫州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he again became Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he returned to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 將行，武帝引朝臣宴別道根于武德殿，召畫工使圖其形，道根踧踖謝曰：「臣所可報國家，唯餘一死，但天下太平，恨無可死之地。」

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, Wudi led court ministers to a farewell feast for Daogen at Wude Hall, summoned painters to portray his form; Daogen, abashed, declined, saying, "What I can repay the state is only my one death—but the realm is at peace and I regret there is no place to die."
translations.idiomatic: Wudi feasted him at Wude Hall and had his portrait painted; Daogen blushed and said he had no war left to die in."

sentences.zh: 豫部重得道根，人皆喜悅。

translations.literal: Yuzhou again obtained Daogen and the people were all joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou rejoiced to have him back.

sentences.zh: 武帝每稱曰：「馮道根所在，能使朝廷不復憶有一州。」

translations.literal: Wudi often said, "Where Feng Daogen is, the court need not remember there is a province."
translations.idiomatic: Wudi said, "With Feng Daogen in office the court forgets whole provinces."

sentences.zh: 居州少時遇疾，乞還。

translations.literal: After little time in the province he fell ill and begged to return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill and asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 朝廷徵為散騎常侍、左軍將軍。

translations.literal: The court summoned him as Regular Attendant and Left Army General.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him as palace attendant and left army general.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 是日，輿駕春祠二廟，及出宮，有司以聞。

translations.literal: That day the imperial carriage was to perform spring sacrifice at the two ancestral temples; when leaving the palace, the authorities reported it.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor was leaving for spring sacrifice when news of his death arrived.

sentences.zh: 帝問中書舍人朱異曰：「吉凶同日，今可行乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Palace Scribe Zhu Yi, "Auspicious and inauspicious on the same day—may we proceed now?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Zhu Yi whether to proceed with the rites on an inauspicious day."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔柳莊寢疾，衛獻公當祭，請屍曰：'有臣柳莊，非寡人之臣，社稷之臣也。

translations.literal: He answered, "Formerly when Liu Zhuang lay ill, Duke Xian of Wei was to sacrifice; he asked the corpse, saying, 'There is the minister Liu Zhuang—not my minister but the state's minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi cited Duke Xian of Wei, who broke off sacrifice for the minister Liu Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 聞其死，請往。

translations.literal: Hearing of his death, he asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Zhuang's death, the duke went at once.

sentences.zh: '不釋祭服而往，遂以襚之。

translations.literal: Without removing sacrificial robes he went and then bestowed burial goods.
translations.idiomatic: He went in sacrificial dress and performed the funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 道根雖未為社稷臣，亦有勞王室，臨之禮也。」

translations.literal: Daogen though not yet a minister of the altars of soil and grain also had toil for the royal house; to go to him was the proper rite."
translations.idiomatic: Daogen, though no pillar of state, had served the house—visiting him was proper."

sentences.zh: 帝即駕幸其宅，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: The Emperor at once drove in person to his house and wept for him exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drove to his home and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Awesome.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name Awesome.

sentences.zh: 子懷嗣。

translations.literal: His son Huai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huai inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 康絢字長明，華山藍田人也。

translations.literal: Kang Xuan, styled Changming, was a man of Lantian in Huashan.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Xuan, courtesy name Changming, was from Lantian in Huashan.

sentences.zh: 其先出自康居。

translations.literal: His ancestors came from Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: His clan originated in Kangju.

sentences.zh: 初，漢置都護，盡臣西域，康居亦遣侍子待詔河西，因留不去，其後遂氏焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Han set up the Protectorate and made all the Western Regions subjects, Kangju also sent a hostage son to wait on edicts at Hexi and therefore stayed and did not leave; afterward they took the surname.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, Kangju sent a hostage prince to Hexi who stayed and founded the clan in China.

sentences.zh: 晉時隴右亂，遷于藍田。

translations.literal: In Jin times when Longyou was in turmoil they moved to Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, turmoil in Longyou drove them to Lantian.

sentences.zh: 絢曾祖因為苻堅太子詹事，生穆。

translations.literal: Xuan's great-grandfather Yin served Fu Jian as Tutor of the Heir Apparent and begot Mu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yin was Fu Jian's tutor of the heir apparent; his son was Mu.

sentences.zh: 穆為姚萇河南尹。

translations.literal: Mu was Yao Chang's Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Mu served Yao Chang as administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 宋永初中，穆率鄉族三千餘家入襄陽之峴南，宋為置華山郡藍田縣，寄立於襄陽，以穆為秦、梁二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Yongchu in Song, Mu led more than three thousand families of the township into the south of Xian at Xiangyang; Song established Huashan Commandery and Lantian County, lodged at Xiangyang, and made Mu Inspector of Qin and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Yongchu era Mu led three thousand families south of Xiangyang's Xian and was made inspector of Qin and Liang.

sentences.zh: 未拜，卒。

translations.literal: Before he was appointed he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking office.

sentences.zh: 絢伯元隆、父元撫，並為流人所推，相繼為華山太守。

translations.literal: Xuan's elder uncle Yuanlong and father Yuanfu were both pushed forward by the displaced people and succeeded one another as Administrator of Huashan.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yuanlong and father Yuanfu, leaders among refugees, each became administrator of Huashan.

sentences.zh: 時魏降人王足陳計，求堰淮水以灌壽陽。

translations.literal: At the time the Wei surrenderer Wang Zu proposed a plan, requesting to dam the Huai to inundate Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei defector Wang Zu proposed damming the Huai to flood Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 足引北方童謠曰：「荊山為上格，浮山為下格，潼沱為激溝，並灌钜野澤。」

translations.literal: Zu cited a northern children's rhyme, saying, "Jing Mountain is the upper frame, Floating Mountain the lower frame, Tongtuo the rushing ditch, together irrigating the great marsh of Juye."
translations.idiomatic: Zu quoted a rhyme: Jing Mountain upper frame, Floating Mountain lower, Tongtuo the sluice—flooding Juye marsh."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，使水工陳承伯、材官將軍祖揯視地形，咸謂淮內沙土漂輕，不堅實，其功不可就。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought it sound and sent hydraulic engineer Chen Chengbo and Material Works General Zu Kai to view the terrain; all said sand and silt within the Huai were light and drifting, not solid, and the work could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi sent engineers who warned the Huai silt was too loose for a dam.

sentences.zh: 帝弗納，發徐、揚人率二十戶取五丁以築之。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not accept it and mobilized men of Xu and Yang, taking five laborers from every twenty households to build it.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored them and drafted five men from every twenty households in Xu and Yang.

sentences.zh: 假絢節、都督淮上諸軍事，並護堰作役人及戰士，有眾二十萬，于鍾離南起浮山，北抵巉石，依岸築土，合脊于中流。

translations.literal: Xuan was lent credentials and made overall commander of military affairs on the Huai, also overseeing dam laborers and warriors, with a host of two hundred thousand; south of Zhongli they raised Floating Mountain, north reaching precipitous stone, building earth along the banks and joining the ridge midstream.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan commanded two hundred thousand men to build a mid-river dam from Floating Mountain north of Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 十四年四月，堰將合，淮水漂疾，復決潰。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year, when the dam was about to close, the Huai current ran swift and again burst and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In month four of year fourteen the Huai tore the nearly finished dam apart.

sentences.zh: 眾患之。

translations.literal: The host was distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The workers despaired.

sentences.zh: 或謂江、淮多蛟，能乘風雨決壞崖岸，其性惡鐵。

translations.literal: Some said the Yangtze and Huai had many flood dragons that could ride wind and rain to break cliffs and banks and by nature hated iron.
translations.idiomatic: Some said river dragons hated iron and wrecked works in storms.

sentences.zh: 因是引東西二冶鐵器，大則釜鬲，小則鋘鋤，數千萬斤沈於堰所，猶不能合。

translations.literal: Therefore they brought iron from east and west smelters, large cauldrons and small hoes, tens of millions of jin sunk at the dam site, yet still could not close it.
translations.idiomatic: They sank millions of jin of iron pots and tools into the breach—it still would not hold.

sentences.zh: 乃伐樹為井幹，填以巨石，加土其上。

translations.literal: Then they felled trees for well frames, filled them with huge stones, and piled earth above.
translations.idiomatic: They drove tree wells packed with boulders and earth into the gap.

sentences.zh: 緣淮百里內岡陵木石無巨細必盡，負擔者肩穿。

translations.literal: Along the Huai for a hundred li within hills and tombs wood and stone great and small were all exhausted; bearers' shoulders were worn through.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred li they stripped hills bare; porters rubbed shoulders raw.

sentences.zh: 夏日疾疫，死者相枕，蠅蟲晝夜聲合。

translations.literal: In summer plague raged; the dead lay pillow to pillow; flies and insects day and night made a single sound.
translations.idiomatic: Summer plague piled corpses; flies droned day and night.

sentences.zh: 武帝湣之，遣尚書右僕射袁昂、侍中謝舉假節慰勞，並加蠲復。

translations.literal: Wudi pitied them and sent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Ang and Palace Attendant Xie Ju with borrowed credentials to comfort and labor them and also grant tax relief.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi sent Yuan Ang and Xie Ju to comfort the workers and grant tax relief.

sentences.zh: 是冬寒甚，淮、泗盡凍，士卒死者十七八。

translations.literal: That winter was very cold; the Huai and Si all froze; soldiers died seven or eight in ten.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Huai and Si froze; seven or eight soldiers in ten died.

sentences.zh: 帝遣賜以衣褲。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent gifts of coats and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent warm clothing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏遣將楊大眼揚聲決堰，絢命諸軍撤營露次以待之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Wei sent the general Yang Dayan proclaiming he would breach the dam; Xuan ordered the armies to withdraw camps and bivouac in the open to await it.
translations.idiomatic: In month eleven Yang Dayan threatened to break the dam; Xuan camped his men in the open to bait him.

sentences.zh: 遣其子悅挑戰，斬魏咸陽王府司馬徐方興，魏軍小卻。

translations.literal: He sent his son Yue to challenge battle and beheaded Wei Xianyang Prince's household steward Xu Fangxing; the Wei army slightly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue killed Wei's steward Xu Fangxing in a skirmish and the enemy pulled back.

sentences.zh: 十五年四月，堰成，其長九里，下闊一百四十丈，上廣四十五丈，高二十丈，深十九丈五尺，夾之以堤，並樹杞柳，軍人安堵，列居其上。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year the dam was completed; it was nine li long, one hundred forty zhang wide below, forty-five zhang wide above, twenty zhang high, nineteen zhang five chi deep; dikes flanked it and they also planted catalpa and willow; the army was settled and ranked dwelling upon it.
translations.idiomatic: In month four of year fifteen the nine-li dam stood; troops camped on its crown.

sentences.zh: 其水清潔，俯視邑居墳墓，了然皆在其下。

translations.literal: Its water was clear and pure; looking down on settlements and graves below, all were plainly visible beneath.
translations.idiomatic: The reservoir was so clear towns and tombs below looked close enough to touch.

sentences.zh: 或謂絢曰：「四瀆天所以節宣其氣，不可久塞，若鑿湫東注，則遊波寬緩，堰得不壞。」

translations.literal: Some said to Xuan, "The four waterways are how Heaven regulates its qi—it cannot be long blocked; if the sluice is cut to flow east, then the wandering waves will be broad and slow and the dam can remain unbroken."
translations.idiomatic: Advisers said opening the eastern sluice would spare the dam by easing the current."

sentences.zh: 絢然之，開湫東注。

translations.literal: Xuan agreed and opened the sluice to flow east.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan opened the eastern outlet.

sentences.zh: 又縱反間于魏曰：「梁所懼開湫。」

translations.literal: He also spread disinformation in Wei, saying, "Liang fears opening the sluice."
translations.idiomatic: He told Wei by rumor that Liang feared the sluice being opened."

sentences.zh: 魏人信之，果鑿山深五丈，開湫北注。

translations.literal: The people of Wei believed it and indeed cut the mountain five zhang deep and opened the sluice to flow north.
translations.idiomatic: Wei believed him, dug five zhang into the mountain, and opened a northern outlet.

sentences.zh: 水日夜分流，湫猶不減。

translations.literal: Water day and night divided in flow yet the sluice still did not diminish.
translations.idiomatic: Water split north and east yet the sluice did not drain.

sentences.zh: 其月，魏軍竟潰而歸。

translations.literal: That month the Wei army at last collapsed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Wei army broke and retreated.

sentences.zh: 水之所及，夾淮方數百里地。

translations.literal: Where the water reached, along the Huai for several hundred li of land on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Floods spread for hundreds of li along both banks of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 魏壽陽城戍稍徙頓八公山。

translations.literal: Wei's Shouyang city garrison gradually shifted to camp at Mount Bagong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's garrison at Shouyang retreated toward Mount Bagong.

sentences.zh: 此南居人散就岡壟。

translations.literal: South of this the inhabitants scattered to hills and mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Southern villagers fled to high ground.

sentences.zh: 初，堰起徐州界，刺史張豹子謂己必屍其事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the dam rose from the Xuzhou border, Inspector Zhang Baozi said he himself must preside over the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When work began, Xuzhou inspector Zhang Baozi assumed he would command it.

sentences.zh: 既而絢以佗官來監作，豹子甚慚，由是譖絢與魏交通。

translations.literal: Then Xuan came as another official to supervise the work; Baozi was very ashamed and from this slandered Xuan as communicating with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was sent to supervise instead; Baozi slandered him as a Wei agent.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不納，猶以事畢征絢。

translations.literal: The Emperor though he did not accept it still recalled Xuan when the work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi dismissed the charge but recalled Xuan when the dam was done.

sentences.zh: 尋除司州刺史，領安陸太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed to Inspector of Sizhou and concurrently Administrator of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Sizhou and administrator of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 絢征還，豹子不修堰，至其秋，淮水暴長，堰壞，奔流於海，殺數萬人。

translations.literal: When Xuan was recalled, Baozi did not maintain the dam; by autumn the Huai swelled violently, the dam broke, and the rush flowed to the sea, killing tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan left, Baozi let the dam fail; autumn floods killed tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 其聲若雷，聞三百里。

translations.literal: Its sound was like thunder, heard three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The roar carried three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 水中怪物，隨流而下，或人頭魚身，或龍形馬首，殊類詭狀，不可勝名。

translations.literal: Monstrous things in the water followed the current down—some human-headed and fish-bodied, some dragon-formed and horse-headed, strange kinds and weird shapes beyond naming.
translations.idiomatic: Monsters swept downriver—fish-headed men, dragon-horses—beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 祖揯坐下獄。

translations.literal: Zu Kai was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Kai was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 絢在州三年，大修城隍，號為嚴整。

translations.literal: Xuan was in the province three years and greatly repaired walls and moats, famed as strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: For three years in office Xuan rebuilt fortifications to renowned strictness.

sentences.zh: 昌義之

translations.literal: Chang Yizhi
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yizhi

sentences.zh: 昌義之，曆陽烏江人也。

translations.literal: Chang Yizhi was a man of Wujiang in Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yizhi was from Wujiang in Liyang.

sentences.zh: 少有武幹，為馮翊戍主。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial talent and was garrison commander of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful and martial, he held the Fengyi garrison.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝為雍州，因事帝，帝亦厚遇之。

translations.literal: When Liang Wudi was in Yongzhou he attached himself to the Emperor through affairs, and the Emperor also treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He attached himself to Wudi when Wudi held Yongzhou and was well treated.

sentences.zh: 及起兵，板為輔國將軍、軍主。

translations.literal: When arms were raised he was appointed General Who Assists the State and army commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the uprising he became a supporting general and army commander.

sentences.zh: 每戰必捷。

translations.literal: In each battle he was sure to win.
translations.idiomatic: He won every battle he fought.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，封永豐侯，累遷北徐州刺史，鎮鍾離。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongfeng and repeatedly moved to Inspector of North Xuzhou, garrisoning Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year one he was made marquis of Yongfeng and inspector of north Xuzhou at Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 四年，大舉北侵，臨川王宏督眾軍向洛口，義之為前軍，攻魏梁城戍，克之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they made a great northern expedition; Prince of Linchuan Hong directed the host toward Luokou; Yizhi was vanguard and attacked the Wei garrison at Liang city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Prince Hong marched north; Yizhi took the Wei garrison at Liang city.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，武帝以征役久，詔班師。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year Wudi, because the campaign had lasted long, issued an edict withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Winter of year five Wudi ordered the northern campaign withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 魏中山王元英乘勢追躡，攻沒馬頭等城。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying seized the moment to pursue, attacked and took Matou and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Prince Yuan Ying pursued and captured Matou and other towns.

sentences.zh: 城內糧貯，魏悉移歸北，議者咸謂無復南向。

translations.literal: Grain stores within the cities—the Wei all moved north; debaters all said there would be no further southward advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei emptied the captured granaries; courtiers thought they would not march south again.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此必進兵，非其實也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "They will surely advance further—this is not real."
translations.idiomatic: Wudi said, "They are feinting—they will come south."

sentences.zh: 乃遣修鍾離城，敕義之為戰守備。

translations.literal: He therefore sent to repair Zhongli city and ordered Yizhi to prepare for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He reinforced Zhongli and ordered Yizhi to ready its defense.

sentences.zh: 是冬，英果率眾數十萬圍鍾離，沖車毀西墉。

translations.literal: That winter Ying indeed led a host of several hundred thousand to besiege Zhongli; assault towers destroyed the western wall.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Ying besieged Zhongli with hundreds of thousands and smashed the west wall.

sentences.zh: 時城中眾才三千，義之督帥，隨方抗禦，前後殺傷萬計，魏軍死者與城平。

translations.literal: At the time the host in the city was only three thousand; Yizhi directed the commanders and resisted according to each direction; before and after they killed and wounded tens of thousands; Wei dead equaled the height of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: With only three thousand men Yizhi directed the defense; Wei losses piled as high as the walls.
