sentences.zh: 六年，帝遣曹景宗、韋叡率眾二十萬救焉，大破魏軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Emperor sent Cao Jingzong and Wei Rui leading a host of two hundred thousand to rescue them and greatly defeated the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: In year six Cao Jingzong and Wei Rui brought two hundred thousand men and crushed the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 義之率輕兵追至洛口而還。

translations.literal: Yizhi led light troops in pursuit to Luokou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi chased with light troops to Luokou and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以功進號軍師將軍，再遷都督、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he advanced in title to General of the Army and was again moved to Overall Commander and Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made army general and overall commander of south Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐以禁物出蕃，為有司所奏免。

translations.literal: He sat because forbidden goods left the frontier and was impeached by the authorities and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for smuggling forbidden goods across the border.

sentences.zh: 十三年，累遷左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was repeatedly moved to Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen he became left guard general.

sentences.zh: 是冬，帝遣太子右衛率康絢督眾軍作荊山堰，魏將李曇定大眾逼荊山，揚聲決堰。

translations.literal: That winter the Emperor sent Right Guard of the Heir Apparent Kang Xuan to direct the host in building the Jing Mountain dam; Wei general Li Tanding led a great host pressing Jing Mountain, proclaiming he would breach the dam.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Kang Xuan built the Jing Mountain dam; Li Tanding threatened to break it.

sentences.zh: 詔假義之節救絢，軍未至，絢等已破魏軍。

translations.literal: Edict lent Yizhi credentials to rescue Xuan; the army had not yet arrived when Xuan and others had already defeated the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was sent to aid Xuan but arrived after Xuan had already won.

sentences.zh: 魏又遣大將軍李平攻硤石，義之又率朱衣直合王神念救之。

translations.literal: Wei again sent Grand General Li Ping to attack Xiashi; Yizhi again led Palace Attendant in Scarlet Robes Wang Shennian to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping attacked Xiashi; Yizhi marched with Wang Shennian to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 魏克硤石，義之班師，為有司所奏，帝以其功臣不問。

translations.literal: Wei took Xiashi; Yizhi withdrew the army and was impeached by the authorities; the Emperor because he was a meritorious minister did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Xiashi fell; Yizhi was impeached but spared as an old hero.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Inspector of North Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen he governed north Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 義之不知書，所識不過十字。

translations.literal: Yizhi did not know books; the graphs he recognized did not exceed ten.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi barely knew ten characters.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，為將能得人死力。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous and broad; as a general he could win men's strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Generous and blunt, he won men to fight to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 及居藩任，吏人安之。

translations.literal: When he held frontier posts officials and people were secure.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier his rule kept officials and people at ease.

sentences.zh: 改封營道縣侯。

translations.literal: He was re-enfeoffed Marquis of Yingdao County.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to Yingdao county.

sentences.zh: 徵為護軍將軍，卒于官。

translations.literal: Summoned as General Who Protects the Army, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as protector of the army, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 帝深痛惜之，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply grieved him; posthumous name Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi mourned him deeply; posthumous name Fierce.

sentences.zh: 子寶景嗣。

translations.literal: His son Baojing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baojing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 論曰：永元之季，雖時主昏狂，荊、雍二州，尚未有釁。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: In the last years of Yongyuan, though the ruler was mad, Jing and Yong had not yet shown rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: In Yongyuan's last years the throne was mad, yet Jing and Yong had not yet rebelled.

sentences.zh: 武皇跡緣家酷，首唱孟津之師，王茂等運接昌期，自致勤王之舉。

translations.literal: Wudi, his traces following family bitterness, first raised the army at Mengjin; Wang Mao and others met a flourishing season and themselves brought the effort of loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi rose at Mengjin on family grief; Wang Mao and others rode the tide of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 若非天人啟期，豈得若斯之速乎。

translations.literal: If Heaven and man had not opened the season, how could it have been so swift?
translations.idiomatic: Without Heaven's nod and men's timing, could success have come so fast?

sentences.zh: 其隆名顯級，亦各風雲之感會也。

translations.literal: Their lofty names and shining ranks were also each a meeting of wind and cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Their fame and rank each matched its moment.

sentences.zh: 元起勤乃胥附，功惟辟土，勞之不圖，禍機先陷。

translations.literal: Yuanqi's diligence was kin joining kin; his merit was opening land; reward was not plotted—yet the engine of disaster struck first.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi's merit in pacifying Shu went unrewarded—disaster struck first.

sentences.zh: 冠軍之貶，於罰已輕，梁之政刑，於斯為失。

translations.literal: The demotion of the general of the champions was light in punishment; Liang's government and punishments at this lost their measure.
translations.idiomatic: Demoting the champion general was too light—Liang's justice failed here.

sentences.zh: 私戚之端，自斯而啟，年之不永，不亦宜乎。

translations.literal: The beginning of private kin favor was from this; a short life was also fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Private favor began here; his early death was no surprise.

sentences.zh: 張惠紹、馮道根、康絢、昌義之攀附之始，其功則末。

translations.literal: Zhang Huishao, Feng Daogen, Kang Xuan, and Chang Yizhi at the start of climbing had merit that was last.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Feng, Kang, and Chang rose late; their great deeds came last.

sentences.zh: 及群盜焚門，張以力戰自著。

translations.literal: When bandits burned the gates, Zhang by force of battle made himself known.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels torched the gates, Zhang distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 鍾離、邵陽之逼，馮、昌勞效居多。

translations.literal: At the press of Zhongli and Shaoyang, Feng and Chang had the greater share of labor and effect.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongli and Shaoyang Feng and Chang bore the heavier fighting.

sentences.zh: 浮山之役，而康絢實典其事。

translations.literal: In the Floating Mountain campaign Kang Xuan truly presided over the affair.
translations.idiomatic: At Floating Mountain Kang Xuan truly ran the work.

sentences.zh: 互有厥勞，寵進宜矣。

translations.literal: Each had his merit; advancement in favor was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Each earned his honors fairly.

sentences.zh: 先是鎮星守天江而堰實興，退舍而決，豈人事乎，其天道也。

translations.literal: Earlier the guardian star held Tianjiang while the dam truly rose; it retreated and the breach followed—is this human affair? It is Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the guardian star held Tian River while the dam rose; it retreated and the breach followed—Heaven's way, not men's.
